definitions.definition: abbreviation for Accident and Emergency: the part of a hospital where people go when they are ill or injured and need treatment quickly
definitions.def_translation: 医院急诊部（Accident and Emergency的缩写）

definitions.definition: an unpleasant or painful situation or person that you have to accept and deal with, although you find it very difficult
definitions.def_translation: 沉重的十字架；烦恼；心理负担

definitions.definition: an occasion when you examine or explain the whole of a subject , method , or piece of work quickly without stopping or getting slower

examples.text: In this book, John Pemble takes a brisk trot through the history and mysteries of Venice.
examples.translation: 在这本书中，约翰‧彭伯简单回顾了威尼斯的历史和神秘之处。

definitions.definition: a lot of something

examples.text: I've got a whole heap of work to do.
examples.translation: 我有很多工作要做。

data.word: a bad workman blames his tools

definitions.definition: said when someone has blamed a mistake or failure on the things that they use to work
definitions.def_translation: 拙匠埋怨工具差，人笨怪刀钝

definitions.definition: a particularly good or successful period of time

examples.text: 2004 was a banner year for astronomy.
examples.translation: 2004年是天文学成果丰硕的一年

examples.text: Technology stocks had a banner month, rising 6.9 per cent.
examples.translation: 各只科技股经历了大好的一个月，上升了6.9%

definitions.definition: a very difficult first experience of something
definitions.def_translation: 初次的痛苦经历;火的洗礼

examples.text: I was given a million-dollar project to manage in my first month - it was a real baptism of fire.
examples.translation: 第一个月就让我管理一个百万美元的项目——这可是个严峻的考验。

definitions.definition: a great number of complaints , criticisms , or questions suddenly directed at someone
definitions.def_translation: 连珠炮一样的（投诉、批评或质问），接二连三的…

examples.text: The TV station has received a barrage of complaints about the amount of violence in the series.
examples.translation: 电视台接到了一连串的投诉，批评电视剧中的暴力镜头太多。

examples.text: He faced a barrage of questions over his handling of the problem.
examples.translation: 就该问题的处理方式，他受到了接二连三的质问。

examples.text: The measures received a barrage of criticism in the financial press.
She has faced a barrage of questions surrounding allegations of financial irregularity.
Proposals for a sugar tax came under a barrage of opposition from the food industry.

definitions.definition: a number of things of a similar type
definitions.def_translation: 一组，一套，一连串（同类事物）

examples.text: In the kitchen an impressive battery of stainless steel utensils hangs on the wall.
examples.translation: 厨房的墙面上挂着一套不锈钢炊具，非常显眼。

examples.text: We were put through a battery of psychological tests.
She faced a battery of questions from reporters gathered outside her home.
He went on TV to deliver a battery of statistics intended to justify his proposals.
The show uses a battery of theatrical effects.

definitions.definition: a pile of one type of food on which other food is arranged as a meal

examples.text: roasted vegetables on a bed of rice
examples.translation: 底下铺了一层米饭的烤蔬菜

examples.text: Serve the beef on a bed of polenta with mushrooms and peppers.
Pile the avocados on a bed of lettuce.
You could serve the fish on a bed of lightly cooked greens.

definitions.definition: something you ask someone to do that will be difficult for them

examples.text: It's a big ask, I know, but we need the project finished by June.
examples.translation: 我知道这个要求令你为难，但是我们需要在六月之前完工。

definitions.definition: a weak and cowardly (= not brave ) man

examples.text: He's just a big girl's blouse.
examples.translation: 他就是一个懦夫（或娘娘腔）。

definitions.definition: a very large number

examples.text: There were billions of flies everywhere.
examples.translation: 到处都有许多的苍蝇。

examples.text: Billions of ads like these are posted on the Internet.
You know that road - we've driven down it a billion times!
There are billions of plastic bags in the cupboard under the sink.
You've got a billion pens - you don't need any more!
I've made billions of cakes like this over the years.

data.word: a bird in the hand (is worth two in the bush)

definitions.definition: said when you recognize that you should not risk losing something you already have by trying to get something you think might be better
definitions.def_translation: 双鸟在林不如一鸟在手。

definitions.definition: a view from a very high place that allows you to see a large area

examples.text: Climb to the top of the Eiffel Tower if you want a bird's eye view of Paris.
examples.translation: 如果你想俯瞰巴黎，就爬到艾菲尔铁塔顶上去。

definitions.definition: too extreme or not reasonable

examples.text: I think it's a bit much for you to expect me to do all the cleaning.
examples.translation: 想让我把所有清扫的活儿都干了——你是不是太过分了。

examples.text: She wore an expensive suit and diamonds, which was a bit much for such a casual restaurant.
examples.translation: 她身穿昂贵的外套，戴着钻石首饰，在这样随意的餐馆显得过分了。

examples.text: Eealier on she liked all the attention but then it got to be a bit much.
I don't know about expecting people to work for ten hours at a stretch - I think it's asking a bit much.
It seems a bit much to ask her to take on caring duties as well as everything else that she does.

definitions.definition: a young man who has sex with a lot of different women
definitions.def_translation: 放荡不羁的小伙子，浪荡公子

definitions.definition: a sexually attractive woman

examples.text: Have you seen his latest bit of skirt?
examples.translation: 你见过他的新任性感女友吗？

definitions.definition: a sexual partner , usually a man, from a low social class
definitions.def_translation: 社会地位低的情人（通常指男性）

examples.text: Jenny's chatting up the barman again. She likes a bit of rough.
examples.translation: 珍妮又在和酒吧侍者搭讪了。她喜欢比她社会地位低的情人。

definitions.definition: a slight but not serious amount or type of something

examples.text: Maria's put on a bit of weight, hasn't she?
examples.translation: 玛丽亚长胖了一点儿，对吧？

examples.text: It's a bit of a nuisance.
examples.translation: 真让人有点儿烦。

examples.text: Getting all the children ready on time can be a bit of a challenge.
The realization that I had left my phone at home sent me into a bit of a panic, but it was fine.
I suppose I felt a bit of envy, too.
It caused a bit of confusion but it was soon sorted out.

definitions.definition: a sexual relationship with someone who is not married to you, or the person you have the relationship with

examples.text: We've thought for a while that he was having a bit on the side.
examples.translation: 曾有一段时间，我们认为他有婚外恋。

definitions.definition: something that is very unpleasant but must be accepted
definitions.def_translation: 不得不吞的苦果；必须接受的严酷事实

examples.text: Losing to a younger player was a bitter pill to swallow.
examples.translation: 输给了更为年轻的对手是严酷的现实。

definitions.definition: a thick covering of something

examples.text: The ground was covered by a thick blanket of snow.
examples.translation: 地上覆盖着一层厚厚的雪。

definitions.definition: something or someone that surprises you because you had almost forgotten about it
definitions.def_translation: （几乎遗忘但现在又看到、听到、遇到等的）令人触动很大的往事，旧物，故人

definitions.definition: something that has a very powerful or noticeable effect

examples.text: The garden is a blaze of colourin autumn.
examples.translation: 秋天花园里姹紫嫣红。

examples.text: His book was launched in a blaze of publicity.
examples.translation: 他的书在大张旗鼓的宣传下上市销售。

examples.text: Last week, the presenter stepped down from his 15-year role on the breakfast show in a blaze of controversy.
She so badly wanted to end her career with a spectacular win - to go out in a blaze of glory.
We watched the sun go down in a blaze of red, orange, and gold.

definitions.definition: something that seems bad or unlucky at first, but results in something good happening later

examples.text: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise really.
examples.translation: 失去那份工作真是因祸得福。

definitions.definition: an idea or answer that suddenly becomes obvious
definitions.def_translation: （主意或答案）在脑海中突然闪现

examples.text: The answer came to her in a blinding flash.
examples.translation: 答案突然闪现在她脑海中。

definitions.definition: a great effort to improve something or do something that needs to be done

examples.text: We had a blitz on the house at the weekend and cleaned it completely.
examples.translation: 我们周末突击打扫了房子，收拾得干干净净。

definitions.definition: a fault that spoils someone's reputation
something such as an ugly building that spoils a pleasant view
a person whose name is very well known to the public

examples.text: The chef is a boldface name in Britain.
examples.translation: 这个厨师在英国是个名人。

examples.text: The scheme attracted thousands of investors, including some boldface names.
examples.translation: 这个规划吸引了成千上万的投资者，其中有一些知名人士。

examples.text: She's dated several boldface names.
examples.translation: 她和几个知名人士约会过。

examples.text: A number of boldface names feature in his diaries.
examples.translation: 他的日记里有很多知名人士。

examples.text: Boldface names have always been used to sell products such as perfume.
examples.translation: 名人常常被用来卖比如香水这样的产品。

examples.text: What was noticeable at the conference was the distinct lack of boldface names.
examples.translation: 这个会议引人注目的一点是明显地缺乏名人（参加）。

data.word: a bolt from/out of the blue

definitions.definition: something completely unexpected that surprises you very much
definitions.def_translation: 出人意料的事情；睛天霹雳

examples.text: The news of his marriage was a bolt from the blue.
examples.translation: 他结婚的消息真是出人意料。

definitions.definition: something that two or more people argue about strongly over a long period of time
the act of telling someone forcefully to start doing something more quickly or actively

examples.text: She's so lazy - she needs a good boot up the backside.
examples.translation: 她太懒了——需要有人好好督促一下。

definitions.definition: the smallest amount of wind

examples.text: There wasn't a breath of air in the room.
examples.translation: 房间里一点儿都不透气。

examples.text: Not a breath of air stirred the trees or the grass.
There were over fifty of us in one small room, without a breath of air.
A few wispy clouds hung in the sky, without a breath of air to move them.
The sea looked like glass that day. There wasn't a breath of air.

definitions.definition: a short period of time spent outside
definitions.def_translation: 在外面稍微呆一会儿;透气

examples.text: I'm just going out for a breath of (fresh) air - I won't be long.
examples.translation: 我去外面透透气 ——很快就回来。

examples.text: I could use a breath of air - I'm just popping out for a second.
We'd been shut in a hot classroom all afternoon and wanted a breath of air.
I took a short walk at lunch just to get a breath of fresh air.
Sometimes it's good to leave the office for a few minutes and get a breath of fresh air.

definitions.definition: someone or something that is new and different and makes everything seem more exciting
definitions.def_translation: 令人耳目一新的人（或物）

examples.text: Angela's so cheerful and lively - she's like a breath of fresh air when she visits.
examples.translation: 安杰拉如此快乐，充满活力——她一来就像带来了一阵清新的空气。

definitions.definition: a situation in which you experience something, or almost experience something, especially something unpleasant

examples.text: Jim had a brush with death (= was nearly killed) on the motorway.
examples.translation: 吉姆在高速公路上差点丧命。

examples.text: Was that your first brush with the law (= experience of being in trouble with the police)?
examples.translation: 那是你第一次和警察打交道吗？

examples.text: It was her brush with mortality - a cancer scare last year - that made Evans rethink her career.
After his latest brush with infamy, the footballer is keen to stay out of the tabloids and is keeping a low profile.
She had a brush with stardom in the eighties as a member of a minor pop band.

definitions.definition: If you give someone a bunch of fives, you hit them hard with your hand closed .
a funny , entertaining person or situation

examples.text: He's not exactly a bundle of laughs, is he?
examples.translation: 他并不是个很滑稽搞笑的人，是不是？

definitions.definition: someone who is extremely nervous and worried
definitions.def_translation: 焦躁的人;紧张不安的人

examples.text: Sorry for shouting - I'm a bundle of nerves these days.
examples.translation: 很抱歉冲你大叫大嚷——这些天我很焦躁。

definitions.definition: sung by a group of people without any musical instruments
definitions.def_translation: （合唱）无乐器伴奏的;团体清唱的

definitions.definition: an example that shows that what you are saying is true or helps to explain why you are saying it

examples.text: Lack of communication causes serious problems and their marriage is a case in point.
examples.translation: 缺乏交流会导致严重问题，他们的婚姻就是个明证。

examples.text: There's a real lack of science teachers. My son's school provides a case in point where an English teacher is now delivering science lessons.
The quality of health care is declining rapidly. Case in point: your mother's recent experience in hospital.
Some can be transmitted without obvious symptoms, this disease being a case in point.

definitions.definition: used when a situation is of a particular type

examples.text: She doesn't want to work full-time, it's a case of having to.
examples.translation: 她不想全日工作，可是不得不如此。

examples.text: The police suspect that it was a case of mistaken identity.
Ultimately, it's a case of weighing the risk against the potential benefit.
Fitness is for everyone. It's just a case of finding an exercise regime that fits in with your lifestyle.
It might have been a case of fatigue or distraction, but the presidential faux pas has continued to make waves.
This isn't just a case of technology being difficult for older users - the design of this phone is genuinely terrible for everyone.

data.word: a change is as good as a rest

definitions.definition: You can get as much good from changing the work you do as from having a rest .
a set of clothes as well as the ones that you are wearing

examples.text: You'll need a change of clothes if you're staying overnight.
examples.translation: 你要是在外面过夜，就需要带一套换洗的衣服。

examples.text: I set off one morning with some food, a bottle of water, and a change of clothes in my bag.
You will need to bring at least two changes of clothes.
Patients on this ward are given a change of clothes daily.
I always keep a change of clothes in my locker at work.

definitions.definition: a criticism or attack on someone that is unfair
definitions.def_translation: 偷偷摸摸的犯规;暗算;奚落

examples.text: I think her making fun of his wife was a cheap shot.
examples.translation: 我觉得他取笑自己的妻子实在不是大丈夫所为。

definitions.definition: a situation in which it is impossible to say which of two things existed first and which caused the other one
definitions.def_translation: 难定鸡与蛋孰先的情况;因果难定的情形

definitions.definition: someone who has been very influenced by a particular period or situation
definitions.def_translation: 深受（某一时期或形势）影响的人

examples.text: Me, I'm a child of the 60s.
examples.translation: 我嘛，是60年代的人。

examples.text: People should never forget that I'm a child of poverty.
He was a child of the Great Depression, who was forced to work from the age of ten.
As a child of the 20th century, it was important to her to understand the era she lived in.
I'm a child of the civil rights movement, and I expect justice for all.

data.word: a chip off the old block

definitions.definition: someone who is very similar in character to their father or mother
definitions.def_translation: （性格上）酷似父亲（或母亲）的人

definitions.definition: a decision by a doctor that someone is healthy

examples.text: He's been given a clean bill of health by the doctor.
examples.translation: 他拿到了一份医生出具的健康证明。

definitions.definition: a decision by someone in authority that a particular thing is in good condition

examples.text: Of 30 countries inspected for airline safety, only 17 received a clean bill of health.
examples.translation: 在对30个国家的航班安全性检查中，只有17个国家获得了安全证书。

definitions.definition: a quick hit on the side of someone's head

examples.text: You do that once more and you'll get a clip round the ear, my lad.
examples.translation: 小子，你再干这种事，我会抽你一耳光。

examples.text: If you take the boy home, his father will give him a clip round the ear.
We'd have got a clip round the ear if we'd left our muddy boots on the floor.
She's an impertinent little wretch who deserves a clip on the ear.
I got a clip on the ear and a lecture about respecting my father's position.

definitions.definition: something bad that almost happened
definitions.def_translation: 侥幸的脱险，几乎发生的坏事

examples.text: The car just missed the child but it was a very close call.
examples.translation: 汽车差点撞着小孩，就差那么一点点。

definitions.definition: something bad that almost happened

examples.text: The car just missed the child but it was a very close thing.
examples.translation: 汽车差点撞着小孩，就差那么一点点。

definitions.definition: a situation or future event that makes you worry or feel unhappy

examples.text: When you're waiting for an operation, you feel like there's a cloud hanging over you.
examples.translation: 等待手术的时候，会感觉忧心忡忡的。

definitions.definition: something that threatens to cause problems or unhappiness in the future
definitions.def_translation: 可能到来的麻烦；令人担忧的事

examples.text: The only cloud on the horizon is the physics exam in June.
examples.translation: 唯一要担心的就是6月份的物理考试。

definitions.definition: a member of a large organization whose job , although necessary , makes them feel as if they are not important
definitions.def_translation: （大机构中的）小职员；不可或缺但无足轻重的人，小人物

examples.text: I decided to set up my own business because I was tired of just being a cog in a machine.
examples.translation: 我决定创立自己的公司，因为我厌倦了在大公司中做个微不足道的小人物。

definitions.definition: a position or view from which a lot of land can be seen
definitions.def_translation: 居高临下的位置（或开阔的视野等）

examples.text: The house occupies a commanding position at the top of the valley.
examples.translation: 这所房子位于山谷顶上一个居高临下的位置。

examples.text: Back then, the town's only recommendation was its commanding position on Lake Ontario.
You can climb to the top of the church tower for a commanding view of the city.
They own over 2,000 acres of land with commanding views of the Pacific Ocean.
The ancient fort has a commanding view of the river to the east.

definitions.definition: a situation in which someone cannot make a fair decision because they will be affected by the result
definitions.def_translation: 利益（或利害）冲突（因为相关自身利益而使当事人无法做出公正或公平判断的情况）

examples.text: I need to declare a conflict of interest here - one of the candidates for the job is a friend of mine.
examples.translation: 我需要报告一个利益冲突的情况——这份工作的候选人之一是我的朋友。

definitions.definition: a combination of words that is nonsense because some of the words suggest the opposite of some of the others

examples.text: Many people think that an honest politician is a contradiction in terms.
examples.translation: 许多人认为“诚实的政客”在用词上自相矛盾。

examples.text: We went on an anarchist march, which is kind of a contradiction in terms.
Many engineers consider sustainable concrete a contradiction in terms.
He has produced a subtle thriller, if that's not a contradiction in terms.

definitions.definition: a victory in which the person or team that wins is much better than the person or team they are competing against
definitions.def_translation: 令人心悦诚服的胜利，大比分获胜

examples.text: They won a convincing victory.
examples.translation: 他们大比分获胜。

examples.text: The Democratic representative retained his seat with a convincing victory over his Republican rival.
It is by no means certain that the coach of England's rugby team will keep his job despite the team's convincing victory last Saturday.
With one point breaking the tie late in overtime, I wouldn't exactly call it a convincing victory.
The world champions need a convincing win over their rivals today in order to get back on track.

definitions.definition: a sudden loss of confidence

examples.text: With inflation at 500 percent, the country faces a crisis of confidence.
examples.translation: 通货膨胀率已达到了500%，该国正面临着信任危机。

examples.text: These poor end-of-year results have led to a crisis of confidence among investors.
The departure of their editor was just one sign of the crisis of confidence at the paper.
The cycling world has plunged once more into a crisis of confidence over the problem of doping.
The king's behaviour led to a crisis of confidence in the monarchy.

definitions.definition: a rude phrase for something that is not true

examples.text: "I'm really sorry!" "What a crock - you are not."
examples.translation: “我真的非常抱歉！”“什么屁话，你根本不是真心的。”

definitions.definition: a way of saying that you need help

examples.text: Most suicide attempts are really a cry for help.
examples.translation: 大多数企图自杀的行为实际上是一种迫切需要帮助的表现。

definitions.definition: someone who is of a higher social class

examples.text: She thinks she's a cut above her neighbours.
examples.translation: 她觉得自己比邻居们高出一等。

definitions.definition: a young woman who is in trouble and needs a man's help
definitions.def_translation: 等待英雄搭救的少女;落难女子

data.word: a delicate situation, matter, point, etc.

definitions.definition: a situation , matter , etc. that needs to be dealt with carefully in order to avoid trouble or offence
definitions.def_translation: 微妙的形势（问题，时刻等）

examples.text: I need to speak to you about a delicate matter.
examples.translation: 我要跟你谈一件很棘手的事情。

examples.text: The pay negotiations have reached a delicate point/stage.
examples.translation: 工资谈判已经到了微妙的关头／阶段。

examples.text: Teachers need to strike a delicate (= carefully achieved) balance between instructing their students and letting them discover things for themselves.
examples.translation: 教师需要在向学生传授知识和引导学生自己去探索之间找到一个微妙的平衡点。

examples.text: This is a very delicate situation, requiring careful handling.
I didn't trust her to approach this rather delicate matter with sensitivity or tact.

definitions.definition: a lot of something

examples.text: The newspaper received a deluge of complaints/letters/phone calls about the article.
examples.translation: 报社收到了关于这篇文章的大量投诉／信件／电话。

examples.text: Not surprisingly, he has faced a deluge of criticism over the comments.
The new laws have created a deluge of paperwork for small companies.
We simply don't have the staff to deal with the deluge of requests for information.
Her comments on the show triggered a deluge of correspondence which we're just working our way through.

definitions.definition: something that you remember slightly , but not very well

examples.text: I had a dim recollection of having met her before.
examples.translation: 我隐约记得以前好像见过她。

examples.text: She had a dim recollection of a tall, bald man who used to visit her parents.
I have a dim memory of the events of that evening but, twenty years after it all happened, it's rather vague.
It was such a long time ago that it's just a dim memory at this point.
He had a dim recollection of a visit to such a house.

definitions.definition: someone who keeps something that they do not want in order to prevent someone else from getting it
something or someone that looks extremely untidy , or something that is very badly done
definitions.def_translation: 乱七八糟的东西；一团糟的人

definitions.definition: a very unhappy and unpleasant life
a plan that has been formally arranged or agreed and that is now certain to happen
definitions.def_translation: 制定好的计划，准备好的计划；板上钉钉的事

examples.text: Although it has yet to happen, reform of the sector is regarded as a done deal.
examples.translation: 虽然这个系统的改革还没有开始，但人们认为这是早晚的事。

examples.text: Many now see the election as a done deal.
They spoke of the project as a done deal.
We hope to reach an agreement but it's very far from being a done deal.
Both parties are keen - it's pretty much a done deal.
These reforms were presented as a done deal.

definitions.definition: a very small amount compared to the amount needed

examples.text: My letter of protest was just a drop in the ocean.
examples.translation: 我的抗议书不过是杯水车薪。

definitions.definition: too much alcohol to drink

data.word: a drowning man will clutch at a straw

definitions.definition: said about someone who is in a very difficult situation , and who will take any available opportunity to improve it
definitions.def_translation: 只要能救命稻草也要抓。

definitions.definition: something unpleasant that cannot be avoided

examples.text: Going bald is just a fact of life.
examples.translation: 谢顶是无法避免的事情。

examples.text: Unfortunately for you, exams are a fact of life.
There's no point complaining about rising prices. They're a fact of life.
Long waits at security checkpoints are a fact of life in this area.
There may be some colleagues you find hard to get on with, but that's a fact of life.

data.word: a fair crack of the whip

definitions.definition: an equal chance to do something

examples.text: It's only right that all the candidates should be given a fair crack of the whip.
examples.translation: 应该给所有候选人平等的机会才合理。

definitions.definition: an opportunity to explain something or give your opinions , without other people trying to influence the situation

examples.text: He didn't think that he got a fair hearing in court.
examples.translation: 他觉得在法庭上没有得到公正的申辩机会。

examples.text: Before making up your mind, you need to give both sides a fair hearing.
He claimed that the company was not given a fair hearing in the press.
She doubted she would get a fair hearing if she went back to her country.
I'm sure the legislation got a fair hearing - I'm just surprised it didn't pass.

definitions.definition: something you do not want to experience because it is so unpleasant

examples.text: When you're 16, an evening at home with your parents seems like a fate worse than death.
examples.translation: 到了16岁，晚上在家和父母呆在一起似乎是极其难受的事。

definitions.definition: an achievement to be proud of

examples.text: It's a real feather in our cap to be playing in the state championship.
examples.translation: 能够参加州锦标赛是真正让我们引以为豪的事。

definitions.definition: a short speech

examples.text: He introduced the visitors with a few well-chosen words.
examples.translation: 他简短地介绍了来访的客人。

definitions.definition: a short distance

examples.text: The museum is just a few steps from the hotel.
examples.translation: 博物馆距离宾馆只有几步之遥。

definitions.definition: a situation in which two groups or people intend to fight until one side has been defeated
definitions.def_translation: 打到决出胜负为止的斗争

data.word: a fine figure of a man/woman

definitions.definition: a person who is tall , with a large , physically attractive body
definitions.def_translation: 身材高大健美的男子／身材高挑动人的女子

definitions.definition: If you say that there is a fine line between one thing and another, you mean that they are very similar . You often say this when one thing is acceptable and the other is not.

examples.text: As a parent, I knew that there was a fine line between panic and caution.
examples.translation: 作为家长，我知道惊慌和谨慎有所不同。

definitions.definition: strong control

examples.text: Reforming these young offenders will require a firm hand.
examples.translation: 对这些少年犯进行改造需要严格的管教手段。

definitions.definition: a person who feels awkward or unhappy because they are in a situation that is not familiar or because they are different from the people around them
definitions.def_translation: 如鱼离水，在陌生环境不得其所

examples.text: I didn't have any friends that were like me. I just always felt like a fish out of water.
He loves being married and if he wasn't he'd be like a fish out of water.
"He was something of a fish out of water here," said a coworker.

definitions.definition: an attempt to discover the facts about something by collecting a lot of information , often secretly
definitions.def_translation: （通常指秘密地）收罗信息、资料（用于调查揭示真相）

examples.text: The investigators' request for the company's accounts is simply a fishing expedition - they have no real evidence of wrongdoing.
examples.translation: 调查员要求查公司的账只是一个收集信息的手段——他们没有违规操作的真实证据。

definitions.definition: a very angry argument in which people shout at each other

examples.text: We had a flaming row over it last night.
examples.translation: 昨晚我们为了这事大吵了一架。

examples.text: Their conversation quickly turned into a flaming row.
A flaming row broke out between two of the ushers just before the wedding was due to start.
I've had some flaming rows with him when he tried to force me to do something I didn't want to do.
The couple were overheard having a flaming row in the hotel bar.

definitions.definition: something that happened only once or for a short time and was not repeated

examples.text: Sadly, their success was just a flash in the pan.
examples.translation: 不幸的是，他们的成功仅仅是昙花一现。

data.word: a flush of anger, excitement, pleasure, etc.

definitions.definition: a sudden strong feeling of anger , excitement , pleasure , etc.

examples.text: Lena felt a flush of shame at the memory.
I can't even think about that without a flush of embarrassment.
He turned on his heel and left the room, feeling a flush of anger.
And what did I feel at the time? Well, a flush of excitement and a bit of anxiety.
I thought I detected a flush of pleasure in her usually calm, composed features.

definitions.definition: something that you would like to be true but that is probably not

examples.text: I waited at home all evening in the fond hope that he might call.
examples.translation: 我等了一整晚，满心期望他会打电话来。

examples.text: Later that year he left for London with a fond hope that he would receive a warmer reception there.
So much for the fond belief that a new manager would breathe life into the team.
People, by and large, have been happy to pay into the system in the fond belief that it would be there for them if they got sick.
Some men do this in the fond belief that it makes them appear younger.

data.word: a force to be reckoned with

definitions.definition: If an organization or a person is described as a force to be reckoned with, it means that they are powerful and have a lot of influence .

examples.text: The United Nations is now a force to be reckoned with.
examples.translation: 联合国现在是一个不可小视的组织。

examples.text: The three-time Oscar winner and mother of four is a force to be reckoned with.
Her natural charisma and popularity make her a force to be reckoned with.
He's certainly a force to be reckoned with in tennis circles.
There's absolutely no doubt that he is a political force to be reckoned with.
It was a performance that left us in no doubt that this former Broadway star is once again a real force to be reckoned with.

definitions.definition: for an even stronger reason than one that has already been accepted
definitions.def_translation: 更加；更有理由，更不容置疑

examples.text: The proposition is incomprehensible to us, and hence a fortiori we cannot be justified in believing it.
examples.translation: 对此提议我们无法理解，因此更加难以信服。

more_examples.text: If the point of minimum marginal cost has not yet been reached, it follows a fortiori that the point of minimum average cost has not been reached either.
There is, a fortiori, no reason why the same word in this Act should not be similarly construed.
Actions generally do speak louder than words: because, paradoxically, they aren't meant to 'speak' at all, and a fortiori aren't meant to speak what's false.

definitions.definition: an opportunity or advantage that someone gets without having done anything to deserve it
definitions.def_translation: 白白得到的东西，无本获得的利益

examples.text: Just because he was the boss's son didn't mean Tim got a free ride.
examples.translation: 就算蒂姆是老板的儿子也不意味着他就能有“免费的午餐”。

data.word: a friend in need is a friend indeed

definitions.definition: This means that a friend who helps you when you really need help is a true friend .

data.word: a full, good, thick, etc. head of hair

definitions.definition: a lot of hair
definitions.def_translation: 很多头发，一头浓密的头发

examples.text: Even as a tiny baby, she had a thick head of hair.
examples.translation: 她还是婴儿的时候就长着一头浓密的头发。

definitions.definition: something that results from something else , or is the way it is because of something else

examples.text: His success is a function of his having worked so hard.
examples.translation: 他的成功是辛勤工作的结果。

examples.text: The low temperatures here are a function of the terrain as much as of the climate.
examples.translation: 这里的低温是地形与气候同时作用的结果。

examples.text: Differences in health outcomes are often said to be a function of socioeconomic disparity.
Variation in water supply is a function of geography.
The amount of water vapour in the air is, in part, a function of temperature.

definitions.definition: a lot of something

examples.text: She has a fund of knowledge on the subject.
examples.translation: 她对这一主题知之甚多。

examples.text: She had a fund of amusing anecdotes about her time working for him.
He could be great company, with a fund of stories from his teaching days.
For all her shortcomings as a politician, there is a fund of goodwill towards her in the party.
He brings to the job a fund of experience in the field.
These people have a fund of local knowledge which is invaluable to us.

definitions.definition: a meeting of rich and famous people
definitions.def_translation: 一群富有的名人;众星云集

examples.text: Present tonight at the long-awaited opening of this film are a whole galaxy of stars from the acting and musical professions.
examples.translation: 人们期待已久的电影首映式今晚举行，一大批影星歌星前来捧场。

examples.text: Italy, with their galaxy of superstar players, are without a doubt favourites to win the contest.
It looks like the French teenager will be the next player to join the club's galaxy of greats.
She was single-handedly responsible for attracting a whole galaxy of writing talent to the publisher.
This small, unassuming town is tonight rolling out the red carpet for a veritable galaxy of stars.

definitions.definition: the best performance that someone is able to produce

examples.text: No one in the team, including myself, brought their A game to any of the matches.
examples.translation: 包括我在内，全队没有人在比赛中发挥到最佳状态。

examples.text: I needed to have my A game today but it wasn't even close.
examples.translation: 今天我需要发挥到最佳状态，但是事实上差太远了。

examples.text: Federer was on his A game and Murray did well to handle him.
examples.translation: 费德勒打出了他的最高水平，而穆雷应对得很好。

more_examples.text: "She is running for reelection," said her representative. "Any challengers out there, you better bring your A game."
He's a prosecutor who knows his stuff. You have to have your A game if you're going up against him.
If she produces her A game she deserves to be involved.
My point is that even if he had his A game going he might have lost.
If they can both take their A games to Centre Court, this is a final of huge possibilities.

definitions.definition: If a sports team has a game in hand over other teams in a competition , it still has another game to play in which it can gain points .

examples.text: Fulham are third from bottom with two games in hand over the teams below them.
examples.translation: 富勒姆排名倒数第三，但是比排名靠后的球队少赛两场。

definitions.definition: an especially good or lucky thing or person that comes to you
definitions.def_translation: 天赐之物（或人）；走运的机会；天上掉下的馅饼

definitions.definition: a type or amount of drink contained in a glass

examples.text: Would you like a glass of water?
examples.translation: 你要不要喝杯水？

examples.text: Two glasses of lemonade, please.
examples.translation: 请给我两杯柠檬汁。

examples.text: I'd love a small glass of orange juice.
He drinks a glass of milk with his breakfast every morning.
He handed me a glass of champagne.
Could you pour me a glass of wine, please?

definitions.definition: an expression in your eyes that shows that you are amused or that you have a secret
definitions.def_translation: （因为开心或心里有秘密而）眼睛发光

examples.text: "I can't tell you that yet, but I will soon," Grandpa said with a gleam in his eye.

definitions.definition: much

examples.text: The new law met with a good deal of opposition at the local level.
examples.translation: 新法律在地方上遭到强烈反对。

examples.text: I should start by saying I have a good deal of sympathy with this campaign.
It has to be said that there's a good deal of scepticism around these claims.
Initially, there was a good deal of confusion about the situation.
The coach endured a good deal of criticism after the game.

definitions.definition: someone who gives you a lot of attention when you are talking about your problems or things that worry you, and tries to understand and support you

data.word: a good time was had by all

definitions.definition: said to mean that everyone enjoyed themselves
a painting or other image of a person that looks very like them
definitions.def_translation: （人物肖像作品等）非常逼真，极其相像

examples.text: Some people didn't think the statue was a good likeness.
We are fairly confident that the police drawing is a strong likeness of the suspect.
The drawing is a good likeness of her father.
The aim of a portrait is not just to capture a convincing likeness, but to show the subject's character.
Are you sure he wasn't the model for this painting? It's a remarkable likeness!

definitions.definition: to be worth /not be worth the price

examples.text: This jacket is a really good buy, at £200.
examples.translation: 这件夹克真合算，才200英镑。

examples.text: A classic blue blazer is always a good buy as it never goes out of fashion.
Linen and cotton goods are generally a good buy, but avoid the fake labels as the quality is usually fairly poor.
Remember that you're paying for quality and that's never a bad buy.
My first house was a bad buy in every respect.
In your opinion, which of these shares is the better buy?

definitions.definition: someone who is good/ bad at meeting new people and talking to them

examples.text: You get to know lots of people at college if you're a good mixer.
examples.translation: 如果你善于交际，在大学里会认识许多人。

examples.text: Ben's a good mixer and loves a party.
He's a nice guy but he's not an especially good mixer.
Shall we invite Millie to the party? Is she a good mixer?
Her school report mentioned that she was a good mixer.
She's a very nice person but, alas, a bad mixer.

definitions.definition: someone who is not/often ill when travelling by boat

examples.text: I wasn't a good sailor at the best of times and the sea was very choppy that day.
Sorry, but I'm not the best sailor. I would rather take a train up the coast, if possible.
Don't worry about me - I'm a good sailor.
I'd never go by boat - I'm a bad sailor.
He wants to join the navy? As bad a sailor as he is?
My brother, who's a bad sailor, was vomiting over the side of the boat.

definitions.definition: an action that helps / harms someone

examples.text: That's my good turn for the day!
examples.translation: 那就算是我今天做的好事！

examples.text: You did me a good turn warning me that Abigail was going to be there.
examples.translation: 你提醒我阿比盖尔要去那儿，真是帮了我大忙。

definitions.definition: a large amount

examples.text: She spends a good deal of her time in China.
examples.translation: 她很多时候在中国。

examples.text: A great deal of effort has gone into making the software reliable.
examples.translation: 已投入大量精力去提高该软件的稳定性。

examples.text: They still need a great deal more money to finish the project.
examples.translation: 他们仍然需要更多的资金才能完成那个项目。

examples.text: It doesn't make a great deal of difference.
A great deal of my time is spent preparing students for exams.
To be honest, a good deal of what she says is just plain common sense.

more_examples.text: We Americans owe a great deal to our European cousins.
I've been in this job for 30 years, and I've picked up a good deal of expertise along the way.
This product has excited a great deal of media interest.
A great deal has been achieved, most notably free elections.
There is a great deal of interest in harnessing wind and waves as new sources of power.

definitions.definition: a lot of similar things or remarks , thrown or shouted at someone at the same time

examples.text: a hail of bullets
examples.translation: 一阵弹雨

examples.text: The prime minister was greeted with a hail of insults as she arrived at the university.
examples.translation: 首相来到大学时遭到一阵辱骂。

examples.text: They army emerged from the castle in a hail of arrows.
He demanded the senator's resignation with a hail of expletives.
They were mowed down in a hail of gunfire.

definitions.definition: a very small distance or amount
definitions.def_translation: 极短的距离，毫厘之差;细微的量

examples.text: His finger was within a hair's breadth of touching the alarm.
examples.translation: 他的手差一点点就碰到警报器了。

examples.text: She came within a hair's breadth of losing her life (= she nearly died).
examples.translation: 她差一点就丢了性命。

definitions.definition: a problem that is very difficult to solve or a person who is very difficult to understand
definitions.def_translation: 棘手的问题；难以理喻的怪人

definitions.definition: a difficult situation to deal with

examples.text: Teachers have a tough row to hoe in today's schools.
examples.translation: 在如今的学校里，老师们的工作很难做。

definitions.definition: the force produced by a large amount of steam in a closed space
a situation in which a person or an activity starts to become very active or successful
definitions.def_translation: 初见成效，开始获得成功

examples.text: They're really beginning to build up a head of steam for their campaign.
examples.translation: 他们的竞选活动正渐显佳绩。

data.word: a health, computer, surf, etc. freak

definitions.definition: someone who is extremely interested in a particular subject or activity

examples.text: You won't be eating burgers with Tom - he's a complete health freak.
She's a fitness freak - running or working out every day.
In his teens he was a computer freak and, left to his own devices, stayed in his room all day.
Chris has turned into a gym freak of late.
He'd assumed I was some kind of yoga freak just because I went to two classes a week!

definitions.definition: a planned meeting between two people who are very interested in having a romantic or sexual relationship
definitions.def_translation: 恋人（或情人）间的约会，浪漫约会

examples.text: I think Carol has a heavy date - she's been in the bathroom for over an hour.
examples.translation: 我想卡罗尔有个浪漫约会——她在洗漱间待了一个多小时。

definitions.definition: a feeling of unhappiness

examples.text: With a heavy heart, she turned to wave goodbye.
examples.translation: 她怀着沉重的心情转身挥手道别。

definitions.definition: used for emphasis to mean "very"

examples.text: It's a heck of a long way to the nearest shop from here.
examples.translation: 从这里到最近的商店也有很长的路。

definitions.definition: a surprisingly good person or thing
definitions.def_translation: 令人惊讶的好人（或好事）

examples.text: 20 dollars for that is a heck of a good deal.
examples.translation: 那只要20美元，真是好买卖。

examples.text: She's one heck of a writer.
examples.translation: 她真是一位好作家。

data.word: a helluva guy, woman, teacher, etc.

definitions.definition: a man, woman, teacher , etc. that you admire very much
definitions.def_translation: 极其喜欢的人／老师（等等）

examples.text: Our new boss is a helluva guy.
I admire my wife because she's a helluva fighter.
He's a helluva guitar player.
My choral instructor is a helluva teacher.
He was a helluva guy who worked for justice all his life.

definitions.definition: a place where a lot of people are working very hard
definitions.def_translation: 繁忙的场所，忙碌的地方

examples.text: The whole house was a hive of activity on the day before the wedding.
examples.translation: 婚礼的前一天，整幢房子里是一派忙碌的景象。

definitions.definition: in golf , an occasion when someone's ball goes into the hole the first time they hit it
a large number of something

examples.text: There's a whole host of reasons why he didn't get the job.
examples.translation: 有一大堆理由可以解释他为什么没有得到那份工作。

examples.text: Their clients were using a host of different advertising methods.
We read works by Swift, Kipling, Waugh, and a host of lesser writers.
Use of these fuels creates a host of environmental and human health problems.
There was a whole host of reasons why the business failed.

definitions.definition: a large number

examples.text: There were hundreds of people at the pool today.
examples.translation: 今天游泳池里人很多。

examples.text: There are a hundred shirts waiting to be ironed.
examples.translation: 有一大堆衬衫要烫呢。

examples.text: I've seen that film hundreds of times.
There are hundreds of banks in this town.
He's been in the same job for a hundred years.

definitions.definition: very many
definitions.def_translation: 非常多的，许许多多的，极多的

examples.text: I can't talk right now - I have a hundred and one things to do this morning.
examples.translation: 我现在不能闲聊——今天上午我有一大堆的事情要做。

definitions.definition: If you give someone a kick up the arse , you do or say something to try to stop them being lazy .
definitions.def_translation: 鞭策；教训，督促（使其不再懒惰）

definitions.definition: a large amount of money

examples.text: That diamond necklace must have cost a king's ransom.
examples.translation: 那条钻石项链一定花了一大笔钱。

definitions.definition: someone who saves you from a difficult or dangerous situation
an event or action that causes someone or something to fail

examples.text: Already out of training, the latest illness has dealt her hopes of a gold medal a knockout blow.
examples.translation: 她本就缺乏训练，最近患病更给她夺金的希望以致命的打击。

definitions.definition: in the style of

examples.text: She has her hair blonde and curly, à la Marilyn Monroe.
examples.translation: 她仿照玛丽莲•梦露的样子，把自己的头发弄成金色卷发。

definitions.definition: If you eat à la carte, you choose each dish from a separate list instead of eating a fixed combination of dishes at a fixed price .

examples.text: You get more choice if you eat à la carte/from the à la carte menu.
examples.translation: 如果你按菜单点菜的话，可选的菜肴会更多些。

definitions.definition: in the most modern style or fashion
served with ice cream

examples.text: apple pie à la mode
examples.translation: 加冰激凌的苹果馅饼

definitions.definition: in the most modern style or fashion
a long list of subjects

examples.text: It wasn't much of a speech - just a laundry list of accusations against the government.
examples.translation: 这不算是演讲，只是在将一连串对政府的控诉罗列起来。

definitions.definition: something you do without being certain what will happen as a result

examples.text: I had very little information about the company, so writing to them was a leap in the dark.
examples.translation: 我对该公司了解得很少，所以给他们写信有些莽撞。

definitions.definition: an act of believing something that is not easily believed
definitions.def_translation: 不易的举动；让人难以置信的做法

examples.text: It took a big leap of faith to decide to quit my job and try something new.
examples.translation: 放弃我的工作尝试新的东西的确不是一个容易的决定。

data.word: a leopard can't/doesn't change its spots

definitions.definition: something you say that means a person's character , especially if it is bad , will not change , even if they pretend that it will
a public exam taken in England and Wales by children aged 17 or 18. Students take AS level exams then A2s , usually a year later , which together make a full A level qualification .
definitions.def_translation: （英格兰和威尔士的中学生在十七八岁时参加的）高级程度考试，高级考试

examples.text: You usually need three A levels to get into university.
examples.translation: 一般要通过3科高级程度考试才能被大学录取。

examples.text: I failed my History A level.
examples.translation: 我的历史高级考试没通过。

examples.text: Do you have an A level in maths?
examples.translation: 你需要参加数学高级程度考试吗？

examples.text: This problem should be easy enough for someone who's done physics at A level.
examples.translation: 对于参加过物理高级考试的人来说，这个问题是很容易的。

definitions.definition: a situation in which everyone has the same chance of succeeding

examples.text: If the tax systems are different in each European country, how can industries start on a level playing field?
examples.translation: 如果欧洲各国的税制不同，那么不同国家的各个行业怎能在均等机会下展开竞争呢？

definitions.definition: a quick and careless act of cleaning or washing

data.word: a list as long as your arm

definitions.definition: a very long list

examples.text: I've got a list as long as my arm of the things we need to do before we leave.
examples.translation: 离开之前我们有一长串的事情要做。

definitions.definition: a long list of unpleasant things, especially things that are repeated
definitions.def_translation: 一连串（反复发生的不愉快的事情）

examples.text: The manufacturers are reported to have received a litany of complaints from dissatisfied customers.
examples.translation: 据报道制造商已经收到了顾客一连串不满意的投诉。

examples.text: He trotted out a litany of woes: bad housing, unemployment, poor health.
She just gave us a litany of excuses for why she hadn't done anything.
The generals made a litany of mistakes early on in the war.
The document was little more than a litany of errors.

definitions.definition: slightly

examples.text: I was a little bit worried by what she said.
examples.translation: 她的话让我有点担心。

examples.text: We'll wait a little longer and then I'll phone them.
examples.translation: 我们再稍微等一等，还不来的话我会给他们打电话的。

examples.text: There's only a little further to go.
examples.translation: 再走一会就到了。

more_examples.text: The ice cream was a little bit sweet for me.
Could you speak a little louder, please?
I'm tired but I can certainly walk a little further.
She's recovering well from her operation, but she's still a little bit shaky on her feet.
Well, you could try to look a little more enthusiastic!

definitions.definition: said if you know who gave you the information being discussed but do not want to say who it was

examples.text: "How did you know he was leaving?" "Oh, let's just say a little bird told me."
examples.translation: “你怎么知道他要走了？”“噢，反正我知道。”

definitions.definition: a small amount of food or drink

examples.text: I always like to have a little something around eleven o'clock in the morning.
examples.translation: 我总喜欢在上午11点左右吃点东西。

examples.text: Can I get you a little something before you set off?
I had a little something at around four o'clock, so I won't need much for supper.
"Are you at all hungry?" "Oh, I could use a little something, thank you."
She always gave me a little something with my afternoon cup of tea.

definitions.definition: a present that is not of great value

examples.text: I want to buy a little something to give to Val when I visit her in hospital.
examples.translation: 我去医院看瓦尔的时候想给她买个小礼物。

examples.text: I think he deserves a little something after all that effort.
I've brought you a little something to say thank you for your help.
Do you think we should get Daniel a little something for his birthday?

data.word: a load of crap, nonsense, rubbish, etc.

definitions.definition: something that is not true , or something of very bad quality
definitions.def_translation: 一派胡言／一堆垃圾（等等）

examples.text: Who said they were cheaper - what a load of rubbish!
examples.translation: 谁说便宜来着——简直就是一堆垃圾！

examples.text: He liked the second series and I thought it was a load of crap.
examples.translation: 他喜欢第二辑，但我却觉得很糟糕。

definitions.definition: an occasion when a problem that has been worrying you stops or is dealt with
definitions.def_translation: 卸下了思想上的重负，心上的石头落了地

examples.text: I'm so relieved that I don't have to make a speech - it's such a weight off my mind!
examples.translation: 不必作演讲让我长舒了一口气——这下我心上的石头可落地了！

definitions.definition: If you have a long face , you look sad .

examples.text: "Why do you have such a long face?" "My boyfriend doesn't want to see me any more."
examples.translation: “你为什么哭丧着脸？”“我男朋友不理我了。”

definitions.definition: something that takes effort over a long time , rather than just a few days , weeks , etc.
definitions.def_translation: 以年记（而不是以天、周、月记）的一段时间

examples.text: The business will not recover quickly; this is the beginning of a long haul.
It's been a long haul, but people appreciate what we've managed to do.
You need to prepare for the long haul.

definitions.definition: a series of people or things that follow each other in time

examples.text: She is the latest in a long line of controversial leaders.
examples.translation: 在一系列颇具争议的领导者中，她是最新的一位。

examples.text: He comes from a long line of doctors (= a lot of his relatives were doctors before him).
examples.translation: 他出身医生世家。

examples.text: This is the latest in a long line of popular talking-animal movies.
He joins a long line of politicians who have promised to tackle corruption.
My mother came from a long line of midwives.

definitions.definition: a lot of work to do or improvements to make
definitions.def_translation: 很长的路要走，很多工作要做

examples.text: He has a long way to go before he can present the plans to the public.
examples.translation: 在将该计划公诸于众之前，他还有很多工作要做。

definitions.definition: lots (of) a large amount or number of people or things

examples.text: She eats lots of fruit.
examples.translation: 她水果吃得很多。

examples.text: There were a lot of people there.
examples.translation: 那里有很多人。

examples.text: He does a lot of travelling in his job.
examples.translation: 他在工作中要跑很多地方。

examples.text: I've got a lot to do today.
examples.translation: 今天我有很多事要做。

examples.text: He earns lots of money.
examples.translation: 他挣钱很多。

examples.text: There's lots of food.
examples.translation: 食物很多。

more_examples.text: It costs a lot to feed and clothe five children.
Try to avoid foods which contain a lot of fat.
We did a lot of cycling in France last year.
This is a very difficult piece of music to play - it demands a lot of concentration.
I can get through a lot more work when I'm on my own.

definitions.definition: a special ability to do something very well
definitions.def_translation: 魔力（可以很好完成事情的特殊能力）

examples.text: The film's success will no doubt please the 46-year-old director, who was rumoured to have lost his magic touch.
examples.translation: 这部电影的巨大成功无疑会令这位46岁的导演非常欣慰，一度传闻他已经失去了他的神奇魔力。

data.word: a man's gotta do what a man's gotta do

definitions.definition: said to mean that you will do whatever you have to do, even if it is difficult or dangerous
definitions.def_translation: 该做的你就得做；上天入地也得做

definitions.definition: a man who enjoys men's activities and being with other men
definitions.def_translation: 男人中的男人（喜爱男性活动、喜欢和男性呆在一起的男子）

examples.text: Terry's what you'd call a man's man - you wouldn't find him at the ballet too many nights a week.
examples.translation: 特里是人们所说的男人中的男人——我想你不可能见他一周好几个晚上都在看芭蕾舞。

definitions.definition: someone who prefers to do things rather than think about and discuss them

examples.text: He was a man of action who believed that to achieve things in life you had to be prepared to fight for them.
Her husband is a man of ideas while she is a practical doctor, a woman of action.

definitions.definition: a man/woman who says very little

examples.text: My father was a man of few words, but when he spoke it was worth listening to.
examples.translation: 我父亲是个少言寡语的人，但他开口时，他的话是值得一听的。

definitions.definition: someone who keeps their promises

examples.text: You can trust him - he's a man of his word.
examples.translation: 你可以相信他——他是个信守诺言的人。

definitions.definition: a rich man/woman

examples.text: You can tell from the clothes she wears that she's a woman of means.
Getting good legal advice isn't a problem for a woman of means.
He thought it essential that he marry a woman of means.
Judging by his yacht and country estate, he is most definitely a man of means.
A man of means, he was able to devote his life to art.

definitions.definition: someone who has a lot of experience of life and people , and can deal with most situations
definitions.def_translation: 阅历丰富的人，老练的人

definitions.definition: a man typical of or involved in marketing , advertising , etc.

examples.text: The brewery's marketing man insisted they were not making a political statement.
As a long-time newspaper man, he knows the effect of budget cuts on journalism.
He had been a hard-nosed Manhattan advertising man before retiring and moving to Vermont.
Marketing men from each bank called their most valuable clients.
The club's president is an advertising man who knows he can sell the club to younger members.

definitions.definition: used when you think that something will happen at some point in the near future

examples.text: If you keep on driving like that, it'll only be a matter of time before you have an accident.
examples.translation: 如果你老是那样开车，迟早会出事的。

definitions.definition: something that you do because it will help you to achieve something else

examples.text: I didn't particularly like the job - it was just a means to an end.
examples.translation: 我不是特别喜欢这项工作——它不过是一个谋生手段罢了。

definitions.definition: a situation when two or more people have the same opinions about something
a symbol that represents a particular thing

examples.text: The author uses disease as a metaphor for the corruption in society.
examples.translation: 这位作家用疾病来比喻社会中的腐败。

examples.text: In the film, the city is a metaphor for confusion and loneliness.
examples.translation: 在这部电影中，城市是迷惘与孤独的象征。

definitions.definition: very quickly

examples.text: Mike was very excited, talking a mile a minute.
examples.translation: 麦克很激动，口若悬河。

definitions.definition: If you can see or tell something a mile off, you notice it easily and quickly .
definitions.def_translation: 一下子，很容易（就能注意到…）

examples.text: She's lying - you can tell it a mile off.
examples.translation: 她在撒谎——你一眼就能看出来。

definitions.definition: a large number

examples.text: I must have told you a million times to close the windows when you leave the house.
examples.translation: 我一定已经告诉你无数次了，离开房间前要把窗子关好。

examples.text: She has millions of friends who could help her.
We've been to London millions of times.
It will be a huge wedding because Aidan's got about a million cousins.
My tummy will never be flat, even if I do a million sit-ups every day.

definitions.definition: someone who has a lot of knowledge

data.word: a miserable, poor, etc. excuse for something

definitions.definition: a very bad example of something
definitions.def_translation: 拙劣的…;蹩脚的…，极糟糕的…东西

examples.text: It was a miserable excuse for a meal.
examples.translation: 这饭真是难吃死了。

definitions.definition: a short time during which someone makes a bad decision or does something bad that they would not normally do
definitions.def_translation: 短暂的失足；片刻的犯错

examples.text: He kept asking me to help him, and in a moment of weakness I said yes.
examples.translation: 他不停地请求我帮他，我心一软就答应了。

definitions.definition: a large amount of something

examples.text: I've got a mountain of work to do.
examples.translation: 我有大量的工作要做。

examples.text: There was a mountain of paperwork to deal with.
By this time, he had amassed a mountain of debt.
All that was left of the apartment block was a mountain of rubble.
We were stuck at the airport with mountain of luggage.
The bridge was by now nothing more than a mountain of debris.

definitions.definition: someone, especially a new baby , who you must provide food for
definitions.def_translation: 需要养活的人（尤指新生儿）

examples.text: They've got three kids and her husband just lost his job - the last thing they need is another mouth to feed.
examples.translation: 他们有3个孩子，丈夫刚失业——绝不想再多养个孩子了。

definitions.definition: an activity that will not make you happy or successful

examples.text: She decided that freelancing was a mug's game.
examples.translation: 她觉得自由职业是件吃力不讨好的事。

definitions.definition: a large number of people or things

examples.text: The city has a multitude of problems, from homelessness to drugs and murder.
examples.translation: 这个城市存在着很多问题，从无家可归到吸毒和谋杀，不胜枚举。

examples.text: This case has raised a multitude of questions.
examples.translation: 这一案例引出了许多问题。

examples.text: There are huge displays of flowers, in a multitude of hues.
He draws from a multitude of disciplines in his work.
The fact is that a whole multitude of factors can affect prices.
It's a sign with a multitude of meanings.

definitions.definition: a situation in which you avoid danger although you very nearly do not

examples.text: We got out in time but it was a narrow escape.
examples.translation: 我们险些未能及时逃脱。

examples.text: There were several narrow escapes from drowning, but somehow each time he survived.
He had a very narrow escape from death when his aircraft came down in a storm.
She had a narrow escape yesterday when the coach that she'd been travelling in careered off the road and ended up upside down in a ditch.

definitions.definition: a success that was almost a failure

examples.text: We caught the ferry but it was a narrow squeak.
examples.translation: 我们险些没赶上渡船。

definitions.definition: a very unpleasant person
something that is impossible or extremely difficult to find , especially because the area you have to search is too large
definitions.def_translation: 不可能（或极难）找到的东西；大海里的针

examples.text: Finding the piece of paper I need in this huge pile of documents is like looking for/trying to find a needle in a haystack
examples.translation: 要在这一大堆文件里找到我需要的那一张纸就像是（企图）大海捞针一样。

definitions.definition: said when someone new takes control of an organization and makes many changes
an occasion when you become more energetic and active than before

examples.text: His grandchildren have given him a new lease of life.
examples.translation: 孙子孙女让他重新变得充满活力。

definitions.definition: an increase in the period for which something can be used or continued
definitions.def_translation: 使用寿命（或持续时间）延长

examples.text: The project suddenly got a new lease of life when the developers agreed to provide some more funding.
examples.translation: 开发商们同意提供更多资金，使这个项目重新燃起了希望。

definitions.definition: the lowest level
definitions.def_translation: 新低／有记录以来的最低点

examples.text: The dollar has hit an all-time low against the Japanese yen.
examples.translation: 美元对日元汇率已经降到了最低点。

examples.text: With interest rates at a new low, this could be a good time to take out a loan.
The dollar is currently heading to a new low against the euro.
The lake's water level has fallen to a record low this spring.
The 749 grey whales counted were a record low.

definitions.definition: an evening when you go to various places and enjoy entertainment such as dancing , eating in a restaurant , or drinking in a bar
definitions.def_translation: 在外玩乐的夜晚，狂欢之夜

examples.text: UKLet's have/go for a night on the town to celebrate.
examples.translation: 让我们狂欢一夜以示庆祝吧。

examples.text: USWe were out for a night on the town to celebrate Dee's graduation.
examples.translation: 为了庆祝迪伊毕业，我们晚上外出狂欢了一夜。

definitions.definition: an evening spent at a restaurant , theatre , etc. rather than staying at home

examples.text: I need a night out with the girls this weekend.
examples.translation: 我这个周末需要跟女生朋友们出去玩一玩。

examples.text: UKLet's have a night out on Saturday.
examples.translation: 我们星期六晚上出去玩吧。

examples.text: I'd like a top that I can wear on a night out.

I was looking forward to a night out with some friends.

definitions.definition: a series of small reductions

examples.text: The department made a nip here and a tuck there, but they were still way over budget.
examples.translation: 这个部门实施了一系列小幅缩减，但他们的开支还是远远超出预算。

definitions.definition: → plastic surgery

examples.text: I suspect she's had a nip and tuck to look like that at her age.
examples.translation: 她这个年纪却有着那样的外表，我怀疑她做过整形手术。

examples.text: It was nip and tuck as to who would win the playoffs.
examples.translation: 加时赛上双方势均力敌，难解难分。

definitions.definition: If a situation is nip and tuck , someone or something in that situation comes very close to failing or ending .

examples.text: For several months it was nip and tuck, but we managed to pull the company out of bankruptcy.
examples.translation: 几个月时间内一直岌岌可危，但是我们成功地把公司从破产边缘拯救了过来。

data.word: a nod is as good as a wink

definitions.definition: used to say that only a slight sign is needed for you to understand clearly what is meant by something or what is happening in a situation
someone that a person has sex with, not because they want a serious relationship , but because they want to have sex with as many people as possible

examples.text: She's not prepared to be just another notch on the bedpost.
examples.translation: 她可不想只成为别人的性伴而已。

definitions.definition: a situation in which the most important factor is how many of a particular thing there are, especially when you disapprove of this

examples.text: To me, business is more than just a numbers game.
examples.translation: 对我来说，做生意不仅仅是个数字游戏。

data.word: a one-time teacher, doctor, cleaner, etc.

definitions.definition: someone who was a teacher , doctor , cleaner , etc. in the past
definitions.def_translation: 曾当过教师／医生／清洁工等的人

examples.text: Duggan, a TV personality and one-time journalist, made the announcement last week.
examples.translation: 这是电视节目主持人、曾做过记者的达根上星期宣布的。

examples.text: The one-time presidential hopeful was among the party.
The one-time school teacher went on to sell millions of records in the 1980s.
The paper had secured an interview with the one-time CEO, who is now living in Spain.
She later fell out with her one-time mentor over money.

definitions.definition: If something is a one-way ticket to an unpleasant situation , it will cause that situation to happen .

examples.text: A rejection of the peace deal would be a one-way ticket to disaster for the country.
examples.translation: 反对和平协议将使国家陷入灾难。

examples.text: These dull, formulaic comedies run for three or four episodes before getting a one-way ticket to television obscurity.

definitions.definition: someone who collects things that they do not need
definitions.def_translation: （收藏的东西都是自己不需要的）垃圾收藏家

examples.text: For me there could be nothing worse than living with a pack rat.
examples.translation: 对我来说，最讨厌的事情，就是和一个垃圾收藏家住在一起。

definitions.definition: an important part of the history of a place , time , or group of people

examples.text: The signing of the peace treaty will be seen as a glorious page in our country's history.
examples.translation: 和平条约的签订将被视为我国历史上光辉的一页。

definitions.definition: someone or something that is very annoying

examples.text: That child is a real pain in the neck.
examples.translation: 那个孩子真讨厌。

definitions.definition: someone or something that is very annoying

examples.text: The kids were a real pain in the arse.
examples.translation: 这些孩子真讨厌。

definitions.definition: the activity of dealing with many different documents in order to achieve something
definitions.def_translation: 文档追索搜集，大量文案工作

examples.text: To receive even the smallest amount of financial aid from a college, it's a real paper chase.
examples.translation: 为获得大学的即使最少量财政补助，也都要先处理填妥数之不尽的文件。

definitions.definition: the point at which two people or organizations separate

examples.text: The parting of the ways came after a series of disagreements between the singer and his song-writer.
examples.translation: 经过一连串争执后，歌手和他的曲作者最终各奔东西。

definitions.definition: a slightly similar appearance

examples.text: He bears more than a passing resemblance to (= he is noticeably similar to) the young Marlon Brando.
examples.translation: 他长得颇像年轻时的马龙‧白兰度。

definitions.definition: an extreme interest in or wish for doing something, such as a hobby , activity , etc.
definitions.def_translation: 对…的热爱，对…的强烈爱好

examples.text: Anton has a consuming passion for science fiction.
examples.translation: 安东对科幻小说痴迷不已。

examples.text: He lives in the countryside and has a passion for beekeeping.

They met at college and shared a passion for clothes and shopping.
They bonded over a shared passion for musical theatre.

definitions.definition: a certain way of getting something you want

examples.text: Many students opt for business studies simply because it sounds like a passport to a good job.
examples.translation: 许多学生选择学商科仅仅是因为它似乎是找到好工作的一种手段。

examples.text: Beauty alone can be a passport to success.
examples.translation: 人们单凭美貌也可能获得成功。

examples.text: He saw the deal as his passport to prosperity.

We need to make these kids realize that education is the passport to a fulfilling life.

definitions.definition: something that is very rare and is considered very important

examples.text: Inexhaustible patience is a pearl of great price.
examples.translation: 无尽的耐心是难能可贵的。

definitions.definition: a mind that understands things quickly and well

examples.text: She had a penetrating mind, capable of incisive thought.
Her penetrating mind soon brought her to academia's attention.
His friends talked of his extraordinarily penetrating mind.
I wish they would apply their penetrating minds to more practical matters.
The work was clearly the product of a penetrating mind.

data.word: a penny saved is a penny earned

definitions.definition: something you say that means it is wise to save money
definitions.def_translation: 小事精明;省一文赚一文

examples.text: I'd advise anyone to put aside a proportion of their earnings - a penny saved is a penny earned.
examples.translation: 我建议人们把收入的一部分存起来——储蓄一文赚一文。

definitions.definition: used to refer to a woman as a sexually attractive object
something that is very easy to do

examples.text: The exam was a piece of cake.
examples.translation: 考试很简单。

definitions.definition: a share of something

examples.text: When the business started making money, everyone in his family wanted a piece of the pie.
examples.translation: 当生意开始赚钱时，他家里所有人都想分一杯羹。

definitions.definition: involvement in something successful that someone else has started
definitions.def_translation: 参与或插手（他人成功之事）；分一杯羹

examples.text: Now research has proved that the drug is effective, everyone wants a slice of the action.
examples.translation: 目前研究证明这种药的确有效，所以大家都想趁机分一杯羹。

definitions.definition: part of the profit or benefit from something, or part of the amount of something that is available
definitions.def_translation: 可以得到的一份（盈利或福利）

examples.text: The company plans to acquire new businesses to grab a bigger piece of the pie.
examples.translation: 公司计划通过兼并来分享更大的利益。

examples.text: People see others getting pay raises and they want a slice of the pie.
examples.translation: 人们看到别人涨工资就想自己也该得一份。

data.word: a piercing criticism, question, remark, etc.

definitions.def_translation: 尖锐的批评／问题／评论等

examples.text: She hadn't really meant to lie, but their piercing questions had forced her to.
examples.translation: 她本不想说谎，但他们尖锐的问题使她不得不这样做。

examples.text: He was famous for his piercing criticism in board meetings.

The report makes some piercing comments about the company's lack of strategic planning.
My mother often made piercing remarks about my appearance.

definitions.definition: something that you buy or accept without first seeing it or finding out if it is good
definitions.def_translation: 盲目购买（或接受）的东西

data.word: a place for everything and everything in its place

definitions.definition: This means that the best way to stay well organized is to keep things in their correct positions .
definitions.def_translation: 物归其所就会干净整洁。

definitions.definition: a good or lucky position

examples.text: He certainly earned his place in the sun.
examples.translation: 他确实得到了一个令人艳羡的位置。

definitions.definition: a large number of things that are unpleasant or likely to cause damage
definitions.def_translation: （令人烦恼或可能造成破坏的）一大群

examples.text: a plague of insects
examples.translation: 昆虫灾害

examples.text: Unfortunately, the bumper harvest was quickly followed by a plague of mice.
A plague of journalists descended on the town.
examples.translation: 一大群记者来到镇上。

examples.text: Computer users all over the world faced a plague of viruses.

definitions.definition: a woman or girl who is not attractive
definitions.def_translation: 平凡的珍妮（不漂亮的女人或女孩）

examples.translation: 如果她象平凡的珍妮，她就不会成为关注的焦点。

examples.text: His wife was a plain Jane with tightly curled hair and a long chin.

She is a resolute plain Jane who doesn't wear make-up or style her hair.
Nobody will give a plain Jane like me a second thought.

data.word: a plume of dust, smoke, etc.

definitions.definition: a tall , thin mass of smoke , dust , or similar substance that rises up into the air

examples.text: After the explosion, a plume of smoke could be seen in the sky for miles around.
examples.translation: 爆炸发生后，方圆几英里都能看得见天空中的烟雾。

examples.text: The plume of smoke and ash was visibible from miles away.

definitions.definition: a problem that politicians from different parties argue about and try to use in order to get an advantage for themselves
definitions.def_translation: 政治足球（各党派政治家争论并试图利用以获取好处的问题）

examples.translation: 我们不想让移民问题成为政治足球。

definitions.definition: in a way that is based on known facts or on what has been seen to happen
definitions.def_translation: 从事实推断原因，由果及因

examples.text: This assumption will be verified a posteriori.

examples.translation: 唯一可行的方法是事后研究系统的演化。

more_examples.text: If the prediction proves incorrect a posteriori, then the natural law claimed a priori also loses all foundation.
The proof of the success of social schemes often comes a posteriori rather than a priori.
