definitions.definition: based on known facts or on what has been seen to happen
definitions.def_translation: 从事实推断原因的，由果及因的

examples.text: This result gives an a posteriori justification of the method used.
This argument is an a posteriori argument.
examples.translation: 这个论证是后验论证。

more_examples.text: Without this a posteriori knowledge, there would be no good reason to make this inference.
Knowledge that is not a priori is called "a posteriori" or "empirical".
With climate change, we have an a posteriori versus a priori argument being played out in the media.

definitions.definition: a lack of something or when the quality of something is extremely low

examples.text: There is a disappointing poverty of creativity in their work.
examples.translation: 他们的工作缺乏创造性，令人失望。

examples.text: The election was marked by a poverty of ideas on both sides.
These young people suffer from a poverty of ambition.
Rents are high because of a poverty of housing stock.
Our national football team has been hampered by a poverty of emerging talent.

definitions.definition: a situation in which one type of person or thing within a set is the largest in number

examples.text: There is a predominance of people with an arts degree on the board of governors.
examples.translation: 理事会中大多数人有文科学位。

examples.text: Sprinters tend to have a predominance of fast-twitch muscle fibres.
His paintings are characterized by a predominance of monochrome tones.
Many seaside areas have a predominance of older residents.
There was a predominance of males among the sickest patients.

definitions.definition: an event that comes before something more important

examples.text: We're hoping these talks could be a preface to peace.
examples.translation: 我们希望这些会谈能拉开和平的序幕。

examples.text: People often deny prejudice as a preface to saying something racist.
Naval ships circled the island as a preface to invasion.
These remarks served as a preface to his announcement that he was leaving the firm.
He used to sling an arm around my shoulder as a preface to asking a particularly awkward question.

definitions.definition: a bad situation

examples.text: Things have come to a pretty pass when a referee can no longer be trusted.
examples.translation: 当裁判不再可信时，情况就很糟糕了。

definitions.definition: a very difficult and annoying situation
relating to an argument that suggests the probable effects of a known cause , or using general principles to suggest likely effects
definitions.def_translation: 由因及果的;由一般到具体的;演绎的

examples.text: "It's freezing outside; you must be cold" is an example of a priori reasoning.
examples.translation: “外面结冰了，你一定会感到很冷” 是一种由因及果的推理。

data.word: a problem shared is a problem halved

definitions.definition: used to say that if you tell someone about a problem , it is easier to deal with
15 minutes

examples.text: I waited a quarter of an hour and then went home.
examples.translation: 我等了一刻钟然后就回家了。

examples.text: I was there three-quarters of an hour.
examples.translation: 我在那里逗留了3刻钟。

examples.text: an hour and three-quarters
examples.translation: 1小时45分钟

examples.text: A quarter of an hour later, Jack arrived.
It should only take a quarter of an hour.
It only takes a quarter of an hour to walk into town.
He only spoke for a quarter of an hour and then took questions from the audience.

data.word: a quarter past two, three, etc.

definitions.definition: 15 minutes after two, three, etc.
definitions.def_translation: 两点/三点/四点等过一刻

examples.text: I'll meet you at a quarter past five.
examples.translation: 我们五点一刻见。

examples.text: I've told Jim we'll see him in the restaurant at a quarter past seven.
I have an appointment at a quarter past ten.
We left at a quarter past nine and were home by ten.
At a quarter past two, she still wasn't here so I called her.
"What time is it?" "It's a quarter after three."

data.word: a quarter to two, three, etc.

definitions.definition: 15 minutes before two, three, etc.
definitions.def_translation: 差一刻两点/三点/四点等

examples.text: It was a quarter to six when I left.
examples.translation: 我离开时差一刻到六点。

examples.text: We get into London at a quarter to four.
She starts school at a quarter to nine.
"What time is it?" "A quarter to ten."
It's already a quarter to eleven.
I'll knock on your door at a quarter to seven, okay?
That cake needs to come out of the oven at a quarter of five.

definitions.definition: an expression used when doubt exists about a particular thing

examples.text: A question mark hangs over the future of the company.
examples.translation: 该公司的前景如何还是个问号。

definitions.definition: someone who is able to learn new things quickly

examples.text: He lacked foreign policy experience but was a quick study.
examples.translation: 他缺乏外交政策方面的经验，但学得很快。

examples.text: Netrebko, who is a very quick study when it comes to languages, speaks English with no noticeable Russian accent.
examples.translation: 涅特列布科学习语言的速度非常快，她说英语的时候没有明显的俄罗斯口音。

definitions.definition: the act of speaking to someone severely or angrily because of something they have done or failed to do
definitions.def_translation: 严厉的批评;厉声的指责;愤怒的谴责

examples.text: I got a rap on the knuckles for not finishing my essay on time.
examples.translation: 我因为没有按时完成论文受到了严厉的批评。

definitions.definition: a large number of unpleasant events of the same type
definitions.def_translation: （一下子出现的）大量令人不快的事

examples.text: There has been a rash of robberies/accidents/complaints in the last two months.
examples.translation: 过去两个月中，突然发生很多起抢劫案／一下出了很多起事故／接二连三收到多起投诉。

examples.text: They have been linked to a rash of kidnappings in the region.
The area has seen a rash of burglaries these past few weeks.
This industry has, in recent years, suffered a rash of bankruptcies on account of cheap imports.
A rash of thefts in the area has left householders feeling anxious.

definitions.definition: bad or unfair treatment

examples.text: He said that many children in the city's schools were getting/being given a raw deal by being taught in classes that were too large.
examples.translation: 他说，城里许多小学生在教育方面没有得到公正的待遇，因为班级人数太多了。

definitions.definition: the act of trying very hard to imagine something

examples.text: It takes (quite) a reach of the imagination to believe that story.
examples.translation: 没有很好的想象力真是难以相信那个说法。

definitions.definition: something that makes other people have a particular opinion about someone or something, especially a bad opinion
definitions.def_translation: 给…带来（尤指不好的）影响的事情；招致对…非议的事情

examples.text: Low test scores are a sad reflection on our school system.
examples.translation: 学生考分低，这使我们的学校系统遭受非议。

examples.text: It's a sobering reflection on our society that there are so many people willing to prey on people's vulnerability.
It's a worrying reflection on the world we live in where people like these are considered to be suitable leaders.
That decent people are treated in this way is a sad reflection on the times we live in.
Her nasty response during the interview was a revealing reflection on the potential liabilities of hiring her.

definitions.definition: a normal man who is liked and trusted

examples.text: He just seemed like a regular guy - like one of us.
He likes to project this image of being a regular guy.
I know he owns multi-million company, but his employees say he's just a regular guy around the office..
He was presented as a regular guy - a family man who loved watching his kids play ball.
He's doing his best to come across as a regular guy, but it's painfully clear he has lived an incredibly sheltered and privileged life.

definitions.definition: a period of time when a ruler controls people in a violent and cruel way
a person or thing that makes you remember a particular person , event , or situation
definitions.def_translation: 使人想起…的东西;引起对…回忆的人;提醒人…的事物

examples.text: Patricia's story is a reminder of how vulnerable women can be in what is still essentially a man's world.
examples.translation: 帕特里希娅的短篇小说提醒人们，在如今实质上仍属于男性的世界里，女性会是多么的易受伤害。

examples.text: The attack serves as a stark reminder of the dangers of doing aid work in this region.
The speech is a timely reminder of our complete dependence on nature.
The memorials provide a poignant reminder of lives lost.
A picture of the doomed vessel hangs on the wall behind him, a constant reminder of the perils of the ocean.

more_examples.text: The monument stands as a chilling reminder of man's inhumanity.
The accident is a grim reminder of the potential dangers involved in North Sea oil production.
The temple ruins are a distant reminder of a vanished empire.
The collapse of the bank is an ominous reminder of the fragility of the world's banking system.

definitions.definition: an occasion when an event or a situation happens again

examples.text: The police hope to avoid a repeat performance of last year, when the festivities turned into rioting.
examples.translation: 警察希望避免去年庆典变成暴乱的事件再次发生。

examples.text: Firefighters are braced for a repeat performance of last year's wildfires.
He won the men's 100m race and is hoping for a repeat performance next month.
You ruined the evening with your tantrum. Let's not have a repeat performance, please.
Anna made me the most wonderful meal - I'm hoping for a repeat performance some time soon!

definitions.definition: a long , narrow piece of something

examples.text: A ribbon of road stretched ahead of us across the desert.
examples.translation: 沙漠中的一条路宛如一根细长的带子，在我们前方延伸。

examples.text: A ribbon of asphalt threads through lush, green fields.
A twisting ribbon of tarmac winds through the mountains.
A ribbon of water divides the city from the forest.
The pizza is topped with ribbons of prosciutto.
The salad was overdressed and topped with tangled ribbons of carrot, carelessly tossed on top of the soggy lettuce.

definitions.definition: someone very annoying or silly

examples.text: We've got a right one here, eh!
examples.translation: “我们这儿有个笨蛋，是不是！”

definitions.definition: extremely colourful and bright

examples.text: Jim's rose garden is a riot of colour.
examples.translation: 吉姆的玫瑰园五彩缤纷。

definitions.definition: the condition of being very old ; used especially to talk about someone who has a long healthy life

examples.text: I'm sure he'll live to a ripe old age.
examples.translation: 我肯定他会高寿的。

examples.text: My grandmother died at the ripe old age of 92.
examples.translation: 我祖母在92岁高龄时去世。

definitions.definition: something that is very successful

examples.text: The party was a roaring success.
examples.translation: 聚会开得非常成功。

definitions.definition: said to mean that a person who is always travelling and changing jobs has the advantage of having no responsibilities , but also has disadvantages such as having no permanent place to live
definitions.def_translation: 滚石不生苔，来去真自在（表示经常在外游荡或老换工作的人可以不用担负责任，但是也居无定所）

examples.text: Hal was a bit of a rolling stone before he married and settled down.
examples.translation: 哈尔以前生活有些漂泊不定，直到婚后才安顿下来。

definitions.definition: a place to live

examples.text: She gave him enough money to get a roof over his head.
examples.translation: 她给他的钱足够他找个住处了。

definitions.definition: a difficult time

examples.text: Government plans to cut sick pay had a rough ride in the House of Commons.
examples.translation: 政府削减病假工资的计划受到了下议院的阻挠。

examples.text: The construction industry is in for a rough ride this year.
examples.translation: 建筑业今年困难重重。

definitions.definition: a cheque (= piece of paper from someone's bank used as payment ) that is not worth anything because the person does not have enough money in the bank
a strange situation or event
one of the stages or levels in something such as a process or organization , through which it is possible to rise or make progress

examples.text: I started my life on the bottom rung of the ladder in this company.
examples.translation: 我从这个公司的最基层干起，开始了我的职业生涯。

examples.text: For her this was just the first rung on her career/professional ladder.
examples.translation: 对她而言这不过是她职业生涯的第一步。

examples.text: Once you rise a few rungs up the ladder, life becomes easier.
examples.translation: 一旦你上升了几个层次，你的日子就会好一些。

definitions.definition: someone who you can trust to do an important job well, without making mistakes

examples.text: Colleagues regard her as a safe pair of hands.
examples.translation: 同事们认为她是一个信得过的人。

definitions.definition: a quick look around a place or area , especially in order to find something
definitions.def_translation: （尤指为寻找某物而）扫视，快速查看

examples.text: I had a quick scout around the house to check everything was okay.
examples.translation: 我迅速查看了一下房子，看一切是否正常。

examples.text: I've had a scout around but I can't see any chairs.
We had a quick scout around the market and think it looks pretty good.
I'll have a scout round the area and see what it's like.
A quick scout around upstairs suggested that there had been a party.
Could you have a scout round and see if you can find them?

definitions.definition: a sudden stop by a vehicle that makes a long , loud , high noise that is unpleasant to hear

examples.text: Eventually, the car came to a screeching halt.
examples.translation: 终于，车子嘎吱嘎吱地停了下来。

examples.text: The train is brought to a screeching halt by a band of outlaws.
examples.translation: 火车被一群不法分子紧急刹停了。

definitions.definition: a sudden and unexpected end to something

examples.text: My young career very nearly came to a screeching halt.
examples.translation: 我年轻的职业生涯几乎戛然而止。

examples.text: Indiana put a screeching halt to Charlotte's five-game winning streak with a 133-96 pounding.
examples.translation: 印第安纳队以 133-96 的比分干净利落地结束了夏洛特队的五连胜。

definitions.definition: a large amount or number of something

examples.text: The teacher looked down and saw a sea of smiling faces.
examples.translation: 老师向下看去，看到一张张微笑的脸庞。

examples.text: It's been raining nonstop here for three days and I'm surrounded by a sea of umbrellas.
The singer looked out over a sea of waving hands.
The floor of the crater melted and turned into a sea of molten rock.
In April, this whole meadow becomes a sea of wildflowers.

definitions.definition: something that has a sudden and positive effect on something, providing encouragement and new activity

examples.text: Fresh investment would provide the shot in the arm that this industry so badly needs.
examples.translation: 新的投资对该行业来说不啻是雪中送炭。

definitions.definition: an attempt to guess something when you have no information or knowledge about the subject and therefore cannot possibly know what the answer is
someone who is willing to listen to your problems and give you sympathy , emotional support , and encouragement
definitions.def_translation: 可以倾诉的对象，可以向其寻求安慰的人

examples.text: I wish you'd been here when my mother died and I needed a shoulder to cry on.
examples.translation: 我母亲去世的时候，你要是在这儿就好了，我当时需要一个可以给我安慰的人。

definitions.definition: a way of saying that you are very pleased to see someone or that you think someone is very attractive
definitions.def_translation: 乐于看到的人;极有吸引力的人

examples.text: You're a sight for sore eyes!
examples.translation: 非常高兴见到你！

data.word: a sledgehammer to crack a nut

definitions.definition: If you use a sledgehammer to crack a nut , you use much more force than is needed .

examples.text: 50 police officers to arrest two unarmed men is surely using a sledgehammer to crack a nut.
examples.translation: 出动50名警察逮捕两个手无寸铁的人，这可真是小题大做。

definitions.definition: A film , piece of literature , or a play might be described as a slice of life if it describes or shows the ordinary details of real life .
definitions.def_translation: 现实生活的写照，反映现实生活的电影（或文学作品、戏剧）

definitions.definition: a large amount of money

examples.text: You'll have to spend a small fortune in legal fees if you decide to sue for compensation.
examples.translation: 如果你决定索赔，要支付一大笔法律费用。

definitions.definition: someone who is skilled at dealing with people and getting what he or she wants from a situation
definitions.def_translation: 圆滑的／精明的人等（尤指善于牟取私利的人）

examples.text: He has shown himself to be a canny operator in wage negotiations.
examples.translation: 他在薪酬谈判过程中表现得精明老练。

examples.text: He proved himself to be a smooth operator in his eight years with the company.
He had a well-deserved reputation as one of the industry's smoothest operators.
She's evidently a clever operator, having surrounded herself with the right sort of people.
She's regarded as one of the smartest operators in the business.
She's a smart operator and don't you forget it.

definitions.definition: a situation in which something increases in size or importance at a faster and faster rate

examples.text: The more successful you become, the more publicity you get and that publicity generates sales. It's a kind of snowball effect.
examples.translation: 你越成功，你的媒体曝光度也高，这种曝光度可产生销售额。这是一种雪球效应。

definitions.definition: If you walk with or have a spring in your step , you walk energetically in a way that shows you are feeling happy and confident .
definitions.def_translation: 步伐轻快;（走路）轻松自信

examples.text: There's been a definite spring in his step ever since he met Joanna.
examples.translation: 自从他遇见乔安娜之后，走起路来步伐都轻快了。

definitions.definition: going back to a worse or less developed state

examples.text: The changes that have been introduced are being seen as a step backwards.
examples.translation: 引入的这些变化被视为一种倒退。

definitions.definition: an improvement or development

examples.text: No one is sure whether this plan will work, but it's a step forward.
examples.translation: 没人说得清这个计划是否会奏效，但它确实是一个进步。

data.word: a stick to beat someone with

definitions.definition: something that you can use to criticize , influence , or cause difficulty for someone or something you dislike or disapprove of

examples.text: The country's lack of openess was used as a stick to beat it with.
examples.translation: 这个国家在公开化上的欠缺经常被人当作把柄。

definitions.definition: said to mean that it is better to act or deal with problems immediately , because if you wait and deal with them later , things will get worse and the problems will take longer to deal with
definitions.def_translation: 及时缝一针能省九针;小洞及时补，免遭大洞苦

definitions.definition: a very short distance

examples.text: The apartment is just a stone's throw from the sea.
examples.translation: 公寓离海非常近。

examples.text: "Is your house far from here?" "No, it's only a stone's throw away."
examples.translation: 你的房子离这儿远吗?"不远，几步路就到了。

definitions.definition: something that is certain to happen

examples.text: The president's re-election is now far from a sure thing.
examples.translation: 总统能否再次当选还远不能肯定。

definitions.definition: used to show agreement

examples.text: "Could you give me a ride home tonight?" "Sure thing!"
examples.translation: “今晚我能搭你的车回家吗？”“没问题！”

definitions.definition: something that no longer happens

examples.text: Giving up your seat to an older person seems to be a thing of the past.
examples.translation: 现在好像很少有人给老人让座了。

definitions.definition: some matters , facts , or information
definitions.def_translation: 一些事情;些许知识，一星半点

examples.text: I'm having trouble paying attention - I have a thing or two on my mind.
examples.translation: 我现在很难集中注意力——我心里有事。

examples.text: Why don't you ask Andrew about it? He knows a thing or two about (= has some knowledge of) computers.
examples.translation: 这个问题为什么不问问安德鲁？他懂点计算机。

examples.text: She thinks she knows everything about raising children, but I could tell her a thing or two (= some information she does not know).
examples.translation: 她觉得自己对于养育孩子样样精通，不过我倒可以让她见识一二。

definitions.definition: a period when you experience a lot of problems
someone who is very unpleasant and difficult to deal with
definitions.def_translation: 讨厌的家伙；难对付的人

examples.text: As a teenager, Jack was a real hard nut, always getting into fights.
examples.translation: 十几岁的杰克很难管教，总是跟人打架。

definitions.definition: an action that makes a bad situation worse , especially one that forces someone to do something

examples.text: Each letter from my bank is another turn of the screw.
examples.translation: 银行的每一封来信都给我带来更大的压力。

definitions.definition: something that is very easy to do, and usually pleasant
definitions.def_translation: 简单易做的事;做起来轻松愉快的事

examples.text: He's used to hard physical work - this is a walk in the park to him.
examples.translation: 他很习惯于做重体力活儿——对他来说是小菜一碟。

definitions.definition: the activity of watching carefully and looking for someone or something

examples.text: Keep a watch out for Nicki and Steve - they should be here somewhere.
examples.translation: 留意一下尼基和史蒂夫——他们应该在这一带。

definitions.definition: a very boring and disappointing experience or person
definitions.def_translation: 无聊（或令人沮丧）的经历；讨厌（或无聊）的人

examples.text: He sounds about as much fun as a wet weekend in Carmarthenshire.
examples.translation: 听起来他在卡马森郡度过了一段很无聊的时光。

definitions.definition: used to refer to a very great amount of something or a very good thing

examples.text: That's a whale of a story.
examples.translation: 那个故事棒极了。

examples.text: Another thousand dollars would make a whale of a difference.
examples.translation: 再有1000美元的话，情况就大不相同了。

definitions.definition: very much

examples.text: Things were about to get a whole lot worse.
examples.translation: 事情就要变得非常糟糕。

examples.text: He didn't like them a whole lot.
examples.translation: 他不太喜欢他们。

definitions.definition: a large number

examples.text: I said no, for a whole lot of reasons.
examples.translation: 我拒绝了，原因很多。

definitions.definition: all of something, or all of the people or things in a group

examples.text: I offered him some chocolate, and he ate the whole lot.
examples.translation: 我请他吃巧克力，结果他全吃了。

examples.text: She's annoyed with the whole lot of you.
examples.translation: 她生你们所有人的气了。

definitions.definition: a completely different situation , often one that is difficult or that you know little about
definitions.def_translation: 完全不同的情况，完全是另一回事儿（尤指难事或自己知之甚少的事情）

examples.text: We'd done a lot of climbing in Scotland but the Himalayas were a whole new ballgame.
examples.translation: 我们之前在苏格兰登过不少山，但攀登喜马拉雅山则完全是另一回事儿。

definitions.definition: a person with a pleasant and friendly appearance that hides the fact that they are evil
If there is a world of difference between two people or things, they are very different.

examples.text: There's a world of difference between the service in the two hotels.
examples.translation: 这两家宾馆的服务有着天壤之别。

definitions.definition: (an example of) illegal noisy or violent behaviour in a public place

examples.text: Ten percent of this group were in persistent trouble for minor breaches of the peace.
This, she said, constituted a serious breach of the peace.
Five other people have been reported for alleged breach of the peace offences.
He was arrested to prevent a further breach of the peace.
UK At Coventry magistrates court she admitted breach of the peace and was bound over in the sum of £300 to keep the peace for one year.

definitions.definition: said when you want to know what another person is thinking , usually because they have been quiet for a while
used to describe something approximately

examples.text: It's a sort of pale orange colour.
examples.translation: 那近乎浅橙色。

definitions.definition: in some way or to some degree

examples.text: I was sort of hoping to leave early today.
examples.translation: 我今天有点儿想早一些离开。

examples.text: It's sort of silly, but I'd like a copy of the photograph.
examples.translation: 这可能有点傻，可这张照片我想要一张。

definitions.definition: the first letter of the English alphabet
a note in Western music

examples.text: This concerto is in the key of A major.
examples.translation: 这支协奏曲是 A 大调。

definitions.definition: a mark in an exam or for a piece of work that shows that your work is considered excellent

examples.text: Sophie got an A for English.
examples.translation: 苏菲英语得了个 A。

examples.text: She got straight As (= all her marks were As) in her final exams.
examples.translation: 她期末考试各科成绩均为 A。

examples.text: Jim is a straight-A student (= all his marks are A).
examples.translation: 吉姆是个全优生。

definitions.definition: used before a noun to refer to a single thing or person that has not been mentioned before, especially when you are not referring to a particular thing or person
definitions.def_translation: 一（个）（用于名词前，表示未曾提及的，尤其是非特指的人、事、物）

examples.text: I've bought a car.
examples.translation: 我买了辆汽车。

examples.text: She's got a boyfriend.
examples.translation: 她交了个男朋友。

examples.text: There was a sudden loud noise.
examples.translation: 突然发出一声巨响。

examples.text: What a shame that you couldn't go to the party.
examples.translation: 你不能去参加聚会，太遗憾了。

examples.text: I heard a child crying.
examples.translation: 我听见有个孩子在哭。

examples.text: Is he a friend of yours (= one of your friends)?

to leave a place , thing, or person , usually for ever

definitions.definition: to stop controlling or managing something that you are in charge of

examples.translation: 她放弃了有关该项目的所有职责。

examples.text: I don't want to abdicate responsibility for any of these problems.
It seems as if the government has abdicated responsibility for the economy.
If you don't speak out, you will be abdicating responsibility for what happens.
Making one person responsible for tackling bullying just encourages others to abdicate responsibility.

definitions.definition: the fact of no longer controlling or managing something that you are in charge of

examples.text: The council denied that their decision represented any abdication of responsibility.
examples.translation: 委员会否认他们的决定是在推卸责任。

examples.text: It is difficult to imagine a more flagrant abdication of duty.
examples.translation: 很难想象还有比这更明目张胆逃避责任的行为。

more_examples.text: It was a shocking abdication of responsibility.
His abdication of presidential authority was observed with mounting concern.
She believes that the pursuit of consensus is the abdication of leadership.
It was an extraordinary time in Nepal, with the declaration of a democratic republic in May and the abdication of the king in June.

definitions.definition: an occasion when a king or queen makes a formal statement that he or she no longer wants to be king or queen
definitions.def_translation: 逊位，退位，让位，正式放弃（王位）

examples.text: The romance between King Edward VIII and Wallis Simpson resulted in Edward's abdication from the throne.
examples.translation: 英王爱德华八世和沃利斯•辛普森之间的恋情导致爱德华退位。

examples.text: His abdication speech was broadcast on the radio.
examples.translation: 他的退位演说在电台上播出。

more_examples.text: It was a shocking abdication of responsibility.
His abdication of presidential authority was observed with mounting concern.
She believes that the pursuit of consensus is the abdication of leadership.
It was an extraordinary time in Nepal, with the declaration of a democratic republic in May and the abdication of the king in June.

definitions.definition: the lower part of a person's or animal's body , containing the stomach , bowels , and other organs , or the end of an insect's body
definitions.def_translation: （人或动物的）腹（部）;（昆虫的）腹部

definitions.definition: in, forming , or relating to the abdomen

examples.text: abdominal pains
examples.translation: 腹痛

examples.text: A membrane covers the abdominal cavity.
examples.translation: 覆盖腹腔的一层膜。

examples.text: This exercise works your abdominal muscles.
examples.translation: 这种练习会锻炼你的腹肌。

more_examples.text: He underwent abdominal surgery last week.
The inner surface of the abdominal wall is pink and shiny.

definitions.definition: muscles in the abdomen
a Latin word meaning "of the abdomen ", used in the names of abdominal muscles , for example the transverse abdominis muscle
definitions.def_translation: （拉丁语）肌肉的（用于腹部肌肉名称中，如transversus abdominis muscle“腹横肌”）

definitions.definition: to force someone to go somewhere with you, often using threats or violence

examples.text: The company director was abducted from his car by terrorists.
examples.translation: 公司董事被恐怖分子从自己的车里劫走了。

definitions.definition: to move a part of the body away from the central part of the body or away from another body part

examples.text: Listen for a clicking sound as the child's hips are abducted.
examples.translation: 听，这个孩子的髋部外展打开时就会发出咔嗒一声。

definitions.definition: a person who is taken and forced to go somewhere with another person , usually with the use of threats or violence

examples.text: These women are all mothers of missing children, thought to be abductees.
examples.translation: 这些妇女都是失踪儿童的母亲，她们的孩子估计是被绑架了。

more_examples.text: She is the mother of a suspected abductee who disappeared 18 years ago.
A man was reported to have been abducted and police later named the abductee as Carlos Lopez.
He argued that strong deterrents were needed to stop a kidnapper from killing an abductee.
The man claimed to be an alien abductee.

definitions.definition: the act of making a person go somewhere with you, especially using threats or violence

examples.text: There has been a series of abductions of young children from schools in the area.
examples.translation: 该地区已经发生了一系列从学校诱拐小学生的案件。

examples.text: He was charged with abduction.
examples.translation: 他被指控绑架。

definitions.definition: the movement of a part of the body away from the central part of the body or from another body part

examples.text: hip abduction exercises
examples.translation: 髋部外展运动

definitions.definition: a person who makes someone go somewhere with them, especially using threats or violence

examples.text: She was tortured by her abductors.
examples.translation: 她受到了绑架者的折磨。

examples.text: It is thought that the woman might have known her abductor.
examples.translation: 据信，这名女子可能认识劫持她的人。

definitions.definition: a muscle that moves a part of the body away from the middle of the body or from another body part
a city in northeastern Scotland
definitions.def_translation: 阿伯丁（苏格兰东北部城市）

examples.text: I was working for an oil company in Aberdeen.
examples.translation: 我当时在阿伯丁的一家石油公司工作。

more_examples.text: Aberdeen has been the northern base for Britain's oil activities since the 70s.
Last year house prices rose 20% in Glasgow, 16% in Dundee, 15% in Edinburgh and 10% in Aberdeen.
700 miles is equivalent to the distance from Aberdeen to Penzance.
Aberdeen businesses back the golf tournament.

definitions.definition: a council area (= area with its own local government ) in northeastern Scotland
definitions.def_translation: 阿伯丁市议会区（位于苏格兰东北部）

examples.text: The 2016 population for Aberdeen City was 229,840.
examples.translation: 2016年阿伯丁市议会区内人口为229,840人。

more_examples.text: The most popular name given to boys born in Aberdeen City last year was Jack.
Compared to Scotland over the period 2013 to 2015, Aberdeen City had a lower death rate.
Aberdeen City Council provides a range of services for people, communities and businesses in Aberdeen.
The BBC hosts a special election hustings for the Aberdeen City council area ahead of the local election on 4 May.

definitions.definition: an area of northeastern Scotland that was a county until 1975 and is now a council area (= an area with its own local government )
definitions.def_translation: 阿伯丁郡（位于苏格兰东北部，1975年撤郡）

examples.text: The route around the northeast coast offers the best of Aberdeenshire and Moray, with rugged cliffs, empty beaches and historic fishing villages.
examples.translation: 东北部海滨沿线是阿伯丁郡和莫瑞的最佳去处，有崎岖的悬崖、空旷的海滩和历史悠久的渔村。

more_examples.text: That area of Aberdeenshire has a long tradition of producing outstanding personalities.
Norman Halkett, a farmer's son, was born in 1910 in Huntly, Aberdeenshire.
In 1715 he landed at Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, during the Jacobite rising.
A committee of Aberdeenshire council rejected the scheme, which was strongly backed by local business but opposed by conservationists.

definitions.definition: a person from Aberdeen, a city in Scotland

examples.text: They discovered that he was an Aberdonian.
Many Aberdonians emigrated to Canada in that period.

more_examples.text: Lindsay, a native Aberdonian, has worked in the offshore industry since 1978.
Aberdonians were well known for their kindness to their neighbours.
As Aberdonians, we were on the same wavelength straight away.

definitions.definition: different from what is typical or usual , especially in an unacceptable way
definitions.def_translation: 违反常规的；反常的；异常的（尤指不能接受的）

examples.text: aberrant behaviour/sexuality
examples.translation: 反常行为／变态性行为

definitions.definition: in a way that is different from what is normal or usual

examples.text: Bats that end up being tested for rabies are generally those that behave aberrantly.
examples.translation: 最终接受狂犬病检测的蝙蝠一般都行为异常。

examples.text: This cell-death process is required for the normal development of the nervous system, but it can be aberrantly activated in neurodegenerative diseases.

more_examples.text: A large number of proteins have been found in excess or to be aberrantly expressed in muscle cells in these patients.
The company has experienced an aberrantly strong first quarter.
The college has produced an aberrantly high number of senior judges.
The researchers found some aberrantly plumaged specimens of the bird.

definitions.definition: a temporary change from the typical or usual way of behaving
definitions.def_translation: （暂时的）脱离常规；反常现象；异常行为

examples.text: I'm sorry I'm late - I had a mental aberration and forgot we had a meeting today.
examples.translation: 对不起，我迟到了。我一时糊涂，竟然忘了今天有会。

examples.text: In a moment of aberration, she agreed to go with him.
examples.translation: 她一反常态，竟然答应跟他一起去了。

examples.text: The misconduct was an aberration from the norm for him.

definitions.definition: to help or encourage someone to do something wrong or illegal
definitions.def_translation: 教唆，唆使，怂恿；伙同…作案

examples.text: His accountant had aided and abetted him in the fraud.
examples.translation: 他的会计与他合谋诈骗。

definitions.definition: the act of helping or encouraging someone to do something wrong or illegal

examples.text: Such acts will be treated as abetment to fraud.
examples.translation: 这种行为会被当成教唆诈骗的。

examples.text: It would be wrong to treat the offence of abetment lightly.
examples.translation: 对教唆行为掉以轻心是不对的。

more_examples.text: Abetment in the offence of murder is as serious the offence of murder itself.
Such activities may be considered abetment to fraud.
A clear case of abetment is made out against him.

definitions.definition: someone who helps or encourages another person to do something wrong or illegal

examples.text: They are all aiders and abettors.
examples.translation: 他们都是帮凶教唆犯。

examples.text: He sounds like every other abettor of terrorism.
examples.translation: 他听起来跟其他恐怖主义教唆犯一个样 。

more_examples.text: Desire for status sometimes leads people to act as abettors of crime.
The abettor of an offence may also be liable to punishment.
They had been abettors of the enemy.

definitions.definition: a state of not happening or being used at present

examples.text: Any proposed abeyance of the bylaws must be approved by the entire committee.
Hostilities between the two groups have been in abeyance since last June.
examples.translation: 自去年6月份以来，双方一直处于休战状态。

examples.text: The project is being held in abeyance until agreement is reached on funding it.
examples.translation: 在达成融资协议前，该项目被暂时搁置。

definitions.definition: to hate a way of behaving or thinking , often because you think it is not moral

examples.text: I abhor all forms of racism.
examples.translation: 我对任何形式的种族主义都深恶痛绝。

definitions.definition: a feeling of hating something or someone

examples.text: She looked at him in/with abhorrence.
examples.translation: 她憎恶地看着他。

examples.text: She has an abhorrence of change.
examples.translation: 她憎恶变革。

definitions.definition: morally very bad
definitions.def_translation: 令人憎恶的;使人厌恶的;可恶的

examples.text: an abhorrent crime
examples.translation: 令人唾弃的罪行

examples.text: Racism of any kind is abhorrent to me.
examples.translation: 我对任何形式的种族主义都深恶痛绝。

definitions.definition: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much:

examples.text: I can't abide her.
examples.translation: 我真受不了她。

definitions.definition: to live or stay somewhere

examples.text: He abided in the wilderness for forty days.
examples.translation: 他在荒野中度过了40天。

definitions.definition: to accept or obey an agreement , decision , or rule
definitions.def_translation: 遵守，遵循（协议、决定或规章）

examples.text: Competitors must abide by the judge's decision.
examples.translation: 参赛者必须服从裁判的裁决。

definitions.definition: An abiding feeling or memory is one that you have had for a long time .

examples.text: My abiding memory is of him in the garden.
examples.translation: 他在花园里的身影永远留在我的记忆中。

examples.text: She holds an abiding affection for her old school.

definitions.definition: in a way that continues for a long time

examples.text: These playwrights are three of the strongest, most individual and most abidingly relevant voices in theatre.
examples.translation: 这三位剧作家是戏剧界最强大、最个性化、最贴近现实的声音。

examples.text: Thanksgiving is one of the most abidingly popular institutions of American culture.
examples.translation: 感恩节是美国文化中历史最悠久的习俗之一。

more_examples.text: Voice, Song and Dance are core elements of Asante culture that abidingly hold and hand down myths and tribal history.
His literary creations are abidingly attractive to highbrow and lowbrow alike.
The play's subject is an abidingly important debate about education and religion.
The effect of the park is abidingly pleasant.

definitions.definition: a large city in the southeastern part of Côte d'Ivoire

examples.text: The company has offices in Abidjan.
examples.translation: 这家公司在阿比让有办公室。

examples.text: The Abidjan airport is just a few hundred yards from the shore.
examples.translation: 阿比让机场离海岸但几百码。

more_examples.text: We arrived in Abidjan the following morning.
He lives in a small town 20 miles from Abidjan.
Women from all over Côte d'Ivoire gathered to celebrate International Women's Day in Abidjan.

definitions.definition: the physical or mental power or skill needed to do something
definitions.def_translation: （体力或智力方面的）能力;才能，才智

examples.text: There's no doubting her ability.
examples.translation: 她的能力毋庸置疑。

examples.text: She had the ability to explain things clearly and concisely.
examples.translation: 她有能力简单扼要地把事情解释清楚。

examples.text: She's a woman of considerable abilities.
examples.translation: 她是个非常有才干的女性。

examples.text: I have children in my class of very mixed abilities (= different levels of skill or intelligence).
examples.translation: 我班里孩子们的能力参差不齐。

examples.text: a mixed-ability class
examples.translation: 不同能力水平的学生混编的班级

more_examples.text: He had no doubts about his team's ability to reach the World Cup finals.
Computer literacy is now as essential as the ability to drive a car.
Organizational ability is essential in a good manager.
Man's ability to talk makes him unlike any other animal.
All the children are taught together in one class, regardless of their ability.

definitions.definition: used to form nouns from adjectives ending in "- able " to mean the quality of being the stated adjective
definitions.def_translation: （用于把以 -able 或 -ible 结尾的形容词转化为名词，表示这些形容词具有的特性）…性

examples.text: suitability
examples.translation: 适宜性

examples.text: vulnerability
examples.translation: 脆弱性

definitions.definition: relating to things in the environment that are not living
definitions.def_translation: 与生物无关的；非生物的

definitions.definition: the state of being extremely unhappy , poor , unsuccessful , etc.:

examples.text: They live in abject poverty.
examples.translation: 他们过着赤贫的生活。

definitions.definition: showing no pride or respect for yourself
definitions.def_translation: 卑躬屈膝的;下贱的;奴性的

examples.text: an abject apology
examples.translation: 低声下气的道歉

examples.text: He is almost abject in his respect for his boss.
examples.translation: 他对老板毕恭毕敬，近乎低三下四。

definitions.definition: the state of being extremely unhappy , poor , unsuccessful , etc.
definitions.def_translation: 极其苦恼（赤贫，极度恐怖等）

examples.text: They live in abject poverty.
examples.translation: 他们过着赤贫的生活。

examples.text: This policy has turned out to be an abject failure.
examples.translation: 结果已经证明这项政策彻底失败了。

examples.text: The news of her death plunged them into abject misery.
He spent the day in a state of abject terror.

more_examples.text: These reforms reduced the number of people living in abject poverty.
They watched in abject despair as their friend was led away.

definitions.definition: in an extreme or bad way
definitions.def_translation: 惨不忍睹地|糟糕至极地

examples.text: The administration had failed abjectly in its duty to protect the country.
examples.translation: 政府糟糕至极，完全没有尽到保护国家的责任。

examples.text: They performed abjectly, losing all four of their matches.
examples.translation: 他们表现得惨不忍睹，四场比赛都输了。

more_examples.text: What went so abjectly wrong?
They are not abjectly poor like some of the people in the village.
It was an abjectly miserable experience.
He said he was abjectly ashamed of his behaviour.

definitions.definition: in a way that shows no pride or respect for yourself

examples.text: "I let you down all the time", he said abjectly.
examples.translation: “我一直让你失望”，他可怜兮兮地说。

examples.text: He abjectly pleaded illness to avoid doing the test.
examples.translation: 他卑鄙地藉口生病以逃避测验。

more_examples.text: What went so abjectly wrong?
They are not abjectly poor like some of the people in the village.
It was an abjectly miserable experience.
He said he was abjectly ashamed of his behaviour.

definitions.definition: to say formally or publicly that you no longer agree with a belief or way of behaving
definitions.def_translation: 公开放弃，声明放弃（信念、行为、活动）

examples.text: He abjured his religion/his life of dissipation.
examples.translation: 他宣布放弃所信仰的宗教／结束放荡的生活。

definitions.definition: to remove body tissue surgically (= by a medical operation )

examples.text: The aim of the operation is to ablate the diseased bowel while preserving normal function.
examples.translation: 该手术的目的是在维持正常功能的同时切除患病肠道。

more_examples.text: Three-dimensional CT models give a map that helps physicians track where they need to ablate tissue.
The cardiologist uses the tip of a special heated wire to "ablate", or destroy, a small area of tissue that is causing the abnormal heart rhythm.
Radiosurgery devices can ablate otherwise untreatable tumors.
Most meteoritic material, by the time it reaches the Earth's surface, has been reduced to dust or to spherules of ablated material in its passage through the atmosphere.

definitions.definition: to remove surface material from a rock , a glacier (= mass of ice ) , etc. by the action of wind , melting , or friction
definitions.def_translation: 消融;侵蚀，（经风化而）销蚀

examples.text: The two comets are entirely ablated before they hit the earth's surface.
examples.translation: 这两颗彗星在撞向地球之前就已经消融殆尽。

more_examples.text: Three-dimensional CT models give a map that helps physicians track where they need to ablate tissue.
The cardiologist uses the tip of a special heated wire to "ablate", or destroy, a small area of tissue that is causing the abnormal heart rhythm.
Radiosurgery devices can ablate otherwise untreatable tumors.
Most meteoritic material, by the time it reaches the Earth's surface, has been reduced to dust or to spherules of ablated material in its passage through the atmosphere.

definitions.definition: the loss of ice or snow from a glacier or iceberg , or the loss of rock or similar material , caused by a process such as melting or erosion (= gradual damage and removing by waves , rain , or wind )
definitions.def_translation: （冰川、冰山）消融;（岩石等物质）融蚀、水蚀

examples.text: Annual measurements have revealed that ice motion and ablation are not uniform from place to place or from year to year.

definitions.definition: the form of a noun , pronoun , or adjective that in some languages , for example Latin , shows by whom or what something is done, or where something comes from
definitions.def_translation: （尤指拉丁语法中的）离格，离格结构

examples.text: These are ablatives after the prepositions ab, de, and ex.

more_examples.text: Many instances of the ablative of cause may be analyzed in two ways: e.g., "vulnere mortuus est" could be understood as "he died from a wound" or "he died by means of a wound".
The ablative after prepositions of place or time denotes location in place and time.

definitions.definition: burning very strongly
definitions.def_translation: 猛烈燃烧的;烈火熊熊的

examples.text: The house was ablaze, and the flames and smoke could be seen for miles around.
examples.translation: 房子燃起了熊熊大火，方圆几英里都能看到烈焰和浓烟。

definitions.definition: brightly lit or brightly coloured
definitions.def_translation: 闪耀的;发光的;明亮的;色彩鲜艳的

examples.text: The ballroom was ablaze with lights.
examples.translation: 舞厅里灯火辉煌。

examples.text: The field was ablaze with wild flowers.
examples.translation: 田野里野花盛开，五彩缤纷。

definitions.definition: full of energy , interest , or emotion
definitions.def_translation: 热烈的；兴致勃勃的；充满激情的

examples.text: Her eyes were ablaze with excitement.
examples.translation: 她激动得双眼熠熠生辉。

definitions.definition: to have the necessary physical strength , mental power , skill , time , money , or opportunity to do something:

examples.text: Will she be able to cope with the work?
examples.translation: 她能应付这项工作吗？

definitions.definition: to find it easier to do something:

examples.text: Get a good night's sleep and you'll feel better able to cope.
examples.translation: 晚上好好睡一觉，就更有能力解决问题。

definitions.definition: intelligent or good at what you do

examples.text: an able child/student/secretary
examples.translation: 聪明的孩子／有才华的学生／能干的秘书

examples.text: This problem is now being looked at by some of the ablest minds/scientists in the country.
examples.translation: 现在国内一些最有才干的人／科学家正在研究这个难题。

definitions.definition: added to verbs to form adjectives that mean able to receive the action of the stated verb
definitions.def_translation: （加在某些动词后构成形容词，表示接受这些动词所表示行为的）可…的，能…的

examples.text: breakable
examples.translation: 易碎的

examples.text: washable
examples.translation: 可洗的

examples.text: movable
examples.translation: 可移动的

definitions.definition: added to verbs to form adjectives that mean worth receiving the action of the stated verb
definitions.def_translation: （加在某些动词后构成形容词，表示值得接受这些动词所表示行为的）值得…的；应…的

examples.text: an admirable person
examples.translation: 可钦佩的人

examples.text: an acceptable answer
examples.translation: 可接受的答案

definitions.definition: in the British and Canadian navies in the past, and in some other navies, a rank held by someone who is not an officer but is more experienced than an ordinary seaman

examples.text: My grandfather was an able seaman on one of HM Navy ships.
The Victoria Cross was awarded to Able Seaman William Savage.
examples.translation: 维多利亚十字勋章授给了一等水兵威廉 • 萨维奇。

more_examples.text: From 1915 he was an able seaman in a destroyer.
She spoke to Able Seaman Chapman.
At that time pay was £11 10s a month for able seamen and £12 for firemen.

definitions.definition: not having a disability (= an illness , injury , or condition that makes it difficult for someone to do some things that other people do)

examples.text: They hold live online forums where viewers from around the world, abled and disabled, can interact.
examples.translation: 他们召开来自世界各地健全的和不健全的观众都可以参与互动的实时在线论坛。

examples.text: The workshops are for abled and disabled dancers.
examples.translation: 这些研讨会是为健全和不健全的舞者开的。

more_examples.text: The participants will be athletes in every field, abled and disabled.
People have so many issues regarding the human body to do with being fat or thin, abled or disabled, black or brown, male or female.
I believe you can teach the same content to a student with a learning disability as to an academically abled student and achieve success.
825 users of the screen reader responded to the survey, consisting of a mix of disabled (90%) and abled users (10%).
The centre will open early next year to meet the needs of less abled people.

definitions.definition: policies , behaviours, rules , etc. that result in unfair or harmful treatment of disabled people (= people who have an illness , injury , or condition that makes it difficult for them to do things that most other people can do) and in a continued unfair advantage to people who are not disabled
definitions.def_translation: （针对残疾人的）体能（或智能）歧视

examples.text: The organization was fraught with institutionalized ableism.
We are grappling with the challenging legacy of ableism.

more_examples.text: Several disabled people have shared their thoughts about the ableism in this book.
We acknowledge that women are oppressed not just by sexism, but by classism, homophobia, racism, ageism, ableism, etc.
He argues that ableism leads us to read the works of writers with mental illnesses exclusively and entirely in the context of their illnesses.

definitions.definition: coming from or having the belief that disabled people (= people who have an illness , injury , or condition that makes it difficult for them to do things that most other people can do) are not as good as people who are not disabled , or that they do not deserve special arrangements that help them to live their lives and be included in society
definitions.def_translation: （针对残疾人的）体能（或智能）歧视的，残疾歧视的

examples.text: The book was criticized for its ableist themes.

more_examples.text: Racist, homophobic or ableist comments are not welcome.

examples.text: You must be absolutely silent or the birds won't appear.
examples.translation: 你必须绝对安静，不然鸟儿就不会飞出来。

examples.text: We've achieved absolutely nothing today.
examples.translation: 我们今天真是一事无成。

more_examples.text: The hotel we stayed in was absolutely superb.
That meeting achieved absolutely nothing - it was a complete waste of time.
My sister absolutely loves chocolate.
The decorations that the children had made were absolutely beautiful.
This case is absolutely full - I can't fit another thing into it.

definitions.definition: used for adding force to a strong adjective that is not usually used with "very" or to a verb expressing strong emotion
definitions.def_translation: （用在通常不和 very 连用的形容词前或表示强烈感情的动词前，以加强语气）确实地;绝对地;极其

examples.text: It's absolutely impossible to work with all this noise.
examples.translation: 噪音这么大，根本没法工作。

examples.text: The food was absolutely disgusting/delicious.
examples.translation: 这食物实在是难以下咽／美味无比。

examples.text: I absolutely loathe/adore jazz.
examples.translation: 我对爵士乐讨厌得要死／喜欢得要命。

definitions.definition: used as a strong way of saying "yes"
definitions.def_translation: （表示强烈赞同）一点不错，完全对

examples.text: "It was an excellent film, though." "Absolutely!"
examples.translation: “不过这部电影棒极了。”“完全同意！”

more_examples.text: The hotel we stayed in was absolutely superb.
That meeting achieved absolutely nothing - it was a complete waste of time.
My sister absolutely loves chocolate.
The decorations that the children had made were absolutely beautiful.
This case is absolutely full - I can't fit another thing into it.

definitions.definition: used as a strong way of saying "no":

examples.text: "Are you too tired to continue?" "Absolutely not!"
examples.translation: “你是不是太累了，无法继续下去了？”“当然不是！”

definitions.definition: used as a strong way of saying "no"
definitions.def_translation: （表示强烈反对）当然不是，绝对不行

examples.text: "Are you too tired to continue?" "Absolutely not!"
examples.translation: “你是不是太累了，无法继续下去了？”“当然不是！”

examples.text: Do we need to be scared? Absolutely not!
Do most students feel this way? Absolutely not, in my experience.
Pay more for the same lacklustre service? Absolutely not!
Has being a woman hindered my career? Absolutely not.

definitions.definition: the act of forgiving someone, especially in the Christian religion , for something bad that they have done or thought
definitions.def_translation: （尤指基督教中的）赦罪，解罪;宽恕

examples.text: She was granted/given absolution.
examples.translation: 她被宽恕了。

definitions.definition: a political system in which a single ruler , group , or political party has complete power over a country
definitions.def_translation: 专制政体;专制制度;专制主义

definitions.definition: ( especially in religion or law ) to free someone from guilt , blame , or responsibility for something
definitions.def_translation: （尤指宗教或法律上）为（某人）解罪;赦免（某人）的罪;宣告（某人）无罪;免除（某人）的责任

examples.text: The report absolved her from/of all blame for the accident.
examples.translation: 那份报告免除了她对那次事故的全部责任。

examples.text: The priest absolved him (of all his sins).
examples.translation: 神父赦免了他（所有的罪过）。

definitions.definition: to take something in, especially gradually

examples.text: Plants absorb carbon dioxide.
examples.translation: 植物吸收二氧化碳。

examples.text: In cold climates, houses need to have walls that will absorb heat.
examples.translation: 在气候寒冷的地方，房屋的墙壁必须能吸收热量。

examples.text: Towels absorb moisture.
examples.translation: 毛巾吸收水汽。

examples.text: The drug is quickly absorbed into the bloodstream.
examples.translation: 药物迅速被血液吸收流遍全身。

examples.text: Our countryside is increasingly being absorbed by/into the large cities.
examples.translation: 我们越来越多的农村地区正被大城市蚕食掉。

definitions.definition: to reduce the effect of a physical force , shock , or change
definitions.def_translation: 消减；缓解（冲力、震动、改变等）

examples.text: The barrier absorbed the main impact of the crash.
examples.translation: 碰撞产生的大部分冲击力被防撞墙吸收了。

more_examples.text: I'm so tired, my poor befuddled brain can't absorb any more.
For running on hard roads, you need shoes with extra cushioning to absorb the shock.
From an early age, children absorb everything going on around them.
He was so absorbed in his work, he hadn't realized everyone else had gone home.
Vitamin D is absorbed by the body after exposure to sunshine.

definitions.definition: to understand facts or ideas completely and remember them

examples.text: It's hard to absorb so much information.
examples.translation: 掌握如此大量信息非常困难。

definitions.definition: to take up someone's attention completely
definitions.def_translation: （使）完全吸引住；（使）全神贯注于…

examples.text: The project has absorbed her for several years.
examples.translation: 好几年她都全神贯注于这项工程中。

definitions.definition: if a business absorbs the cost of something, it pays that cost easily

examples.text: The school has absorbed most of the expenses so far, but it may have to offer fewer places next year to reduce costs.
examples.translation: 这间学校目前能够承担大部分的费用，可是明年可能不得不通过减少招生降低开支。

definitions.definition: if one company absorbs another company , it takes control of it and they become one company

examples.text: Telecorp Holdings absorbed its Spanish subsidiary into its British headquarters.
examples.translation: 泰利控股将其西班牙子公司并入英国总部。

definitions.definition: An absorbable substance can be absorbed , especially by the body .
definitions.def_translation: 可吸收的;能被身体吸收的

examples.text: Fizzy drinks provide readily absorbable sugar and lead to a rapid increase in glucose levels.
examples.translation: 碳酸饮料提供易被吸收的糖分，并导致血糖水平迅速升高。

examples.text: Cooking makes nutrients like beta-carotene and lycopene more absorbable.
examples.translation: 烹煮使β-胡萝卜素和番茄红素等营养物质更容易被人体吸收。

examples.text: They knew that some dangerous gases were absorbable through the skin.
examples.translation: 他们知道一些危险气体可以通过皮肤吸收。

more_examples.text: They changed her nutritional supplement to one with a more absorbable form of iron.
The wound is sutured with absorbable material.
Though not absorbable through the skin, lead and other heavy metals can be vaporized and breathed in as a particulate dust.
The absorbable stent is composed of a biodegradable polyester that slowly releases the drug.
Instantly absorbable, this cream will leave your hands feeling fresh and fragrant.

definitions.definition: very interested in something and not paying attention to anything else
definitions.def_translation: 被…吸引住；专心致志于；全神贯注于

examples.text: Simon was so absorbed in his book that he didn't even notice me come in.
examples.translation: 西蒙读书太入神了，我进来他都没有注意到。

definitions.definition: the ability to absorb liquid
able to take liquid in through the surface and to hold it

examples.text: absorbent paper
examples.translation: 吸水纸

definitions.definition: Something that is absorbing is very interesting and keeps your attention .

examples.text: I read her last novel and found it very absorbing.
examples.translation: 我读了她最新一本小说，觉得非常吸引人。

definitions.definition: the process of taking something into another substance

examples.text: Some poisonous gases can enter the body by absorption through the skin.
examples.translation: 一些有毒气体可以通过皮肤吸收进入体内。

definitions.definition: complete interest in something

examples.text: Her absorption in her work is so great that she thinks about nothing else.
examples.translation: 她工作专心致志，心无旁骛。

definitions.definition: the situation in which a company pays the cost of something easily

examples.text: We can justify the company's absorption of higher manufacturing costs.
examples.translation: 我们可以证明公司支付更高的制作成本是合理的。

definitions.definition: the situation in which one company takes control of another so that they become one company

examples.text: Reports confirmed the absorption of Kode's operations into DCM's offices.
examples.translation: 有报道确认Kode的业务已被并入DCM公司。

definitions.definition: able to take liquids or other substances in through a surface and to hold them

examples.text: The compound is formed so that it can enable uptake by absorptive cells.
examples.translation: 形成化合物，使有吸收能力的细胞开始摄入。

examples.text: the absorptive surfaces of the small intestine
examples.translation: 小肠的吸收表层

more_examples.text: Because of its absorptive properties, tapioca flour is often used as a thickening agent in recipes.
A physical obstruction can be caused by matter attached to the absorptive layer of the bowel wall.
Compression garments and absorptive pads are applied for the immediate postoperative period.
Acoustic problems might be caused by a ceiling that's too high or absorptive to bounce the laughter around.
Acai is rich in a highly absorptive form of calcium.

definitions.definition: able to be absorbed (= taken in and held or used) , for example by the skin or the body

examples.text: The small molecules of goat's milk make it highly absorptive when rubbed into the skin.
examples.translation: 揉入皮肤时，山羊奶的小分子使其非常容易被吸收。

examples.text: absorptive vitamins and minerals
examples.translation: 可被吸收的维生素和矿物质

more_examples.text: Because of its absorptive properties, tapioca flour is often used as a thickening agent in recipes.

definitions.definition: the ability to take liquids or other substances in through a surface and to hold or use them, or the amount of a liquid or other substance that can be taken in like this
definitions.def_translation: （对液体等的）吸收能力;（对液体等的）吸收量

examples.text: Metal surfaces vary in smoothness, absorptive capacity, and chemical reactivity.
examples.translation: 金属表面的光滑度、吸收能力和化学反应性均不尽相同。

examples.text: How do we best make use of the atmosphere's limited absorptive capacity for greenhouse gases?
examples.translation: 我们怎么才能在温室气体方面最好地利用大气层吸收能力的限度？

more_examples.text: The plants are unable to obtain water from the soil: their roots have limited absorptive capacities, and are generally only used for anchorage.
The normal absorptive capacity of the colon is estimated to be as much as six litres per day.
A balanced diet should be enough to meet the body's normal absorptive capacity for vitamins.
He says there are limits to how much oil revenue Gulf countries can absorb, adding that the region is already operating at its maximum absorptive capacity.
The firm's strength in R&D has enabled it to have the absorptive capacity to appropriate the scientific discoveries made overseas.
The more specific the knowledge is, people will take more time or will require better absorptive capacities to acquire it.

definitions.definition: the amount of something or the number of people that an area or place is able to take in and deal with

examples.text: The refugee problem is likely to get worse, partly because the absorptive capacity of the area is limited.
examples.translation: 难民问题很有可能恶化，部分原因是该地区的容纳能力是有限的。

definitions.def_translation: （某机构对新方法或科技等的）吸收能力

examples.text: The development of absorptive capacity is important in enabling firms to use research and technology generated externally.
examples.translation: 增强吸收能力在使公司得以利用外部研究和技术方面十分重要。

definitions.def_translation: （某人对事实、观点等的）吸收能力，理解能力

examples.text: You possess a great absorptive capacity and the power to memorize.
examples.translation: 你具有非常强大的理解力和记忆力。

examples.text: The study looked at the thermal absorptivity of nanoporous materials.
examples.translation: 这项研究考察了纳米多孔材料的热吸收性能。

examples.text: The new coating creates a surface with excellent absorptivity.

more_examples.text: Longer-wavelength radiation would have a higher absorptivity and would be absorbed in the outer layers 0f the sample.

The reformulated ointment has improved absorptivity of its active ingredient.

definitions.definition: the ability of a substance to be absorbed (= taken in and held or used) , for example by the skin or the body

examples.text: They measured the absorptivity of three different moisturizing creams.
examples.translation: 他们测量了三种不同保湿霜的吸收性。

examples.text: The study looks at the factors affecting the absorptivity of nutrients.

more_examples.text: Longer-wavelength radiation would have a higher absorptivity and would be absorbed in the outer layers 0f the sample.

The reformulated ointment has improved absorptivity of its active ingredient.

definitions.definition: to leave suddenly
to not do something, especially something enjoyable that you think might be bad
definitions.def_translation: 节制；戒绝（尤指不好的享乐）

examples.text: He took a vow to abstain from alcohol/smoking/sex.
examples.translation: 他发誓戒酒／戒烟／禁欲。

definitions.definition: to decide not to use your vote

examples.text: 63 members voted in favour, 39 opposed, and 15 abstained.
examples.translation: 63名成员投票赞成，39票反对，15票弃权。

definitions.definition: to stay away from work

examples.text: During a recent general strike, employees of all major trade unions abstained.
examples.translation: 在最近一次大型罢工期间，所有大型工会的成员都拒绝工作。

definitions.definition: someone who does not do something, especially something they would like to do

examples.text: His grandfather was a lifelong abstainer who never touched a drop of alcohol.
examples.translation: 他祖父一生都是一个滴酒不沾的禁欲者。

examples.text: Animal rights should extend to geese, say French foie gras abstainers.
examples.translation: 动物权益(保护）应该扩展到鹅类，不吃法国鹅肝的人说。

more_examples.text: Abstainers do not necessarily enjoy better health than moderate drinkers.
Jimmy Carter and both Presidents George Bush were reportedly abstainers, but Bill Clinton liked cigars from time to time.
The government may lose the vote if there are too many abstainers.

definitions.definition: not doing things that give you pleasure , especially not eating good food or drinking alcohol
definitions.def_translation: （尤指对美食或饮酒）有节制的；戒绝的

definitions.definition: avoiding things that give pleasure but may be bad for you, for example eating too much or drinking alcohol

examples.text: Smith celebrated abstemiously with two of his closest friends.
examples.translation: 史密斯不铺张地和两个最亲近的朋友庆祝了一下。

examples.text: He performed his duties assiduously and lived abstemiously.
examples.translation: 他兢兢业业地做好本职工作，但生活得非常节制。

more_examples.text: Desserts are allowed when you are on a diet, but they should be eaten abstemiously.
The thought is enough to drive you to drink but Alison soldiers abstemiously on.
The author defines the middle class abstemiously, as those who spend $3 -10 a day.

definitions.definition: the fact of not voting in favour of or against someone or something

examples.text: There were high levels of abstention (from voting) in the last elections.
examples.translation: 上几次选举中都有很多人放弃了投票权。

examples.text: There were ten votes in favour, six against, and three abstentions.
examples.translation: 10票赞成，6票反对，3票弃权。

definitions.definition: not doing something, such as drinking alcohol or having sex
definitions.def_translation: 节制；戒绝（如饮酒，性行为等）

examples.text: Abstention from alcohol is essential while you are taking this medication.
examples.translation: 服用这种药物期间，一定要戒酒。

definitions.definition: the fact of not doing something, usually something that is considered harmful such as drinking alcohol or using a drug

examples.text: We found that with abstinence from smoking, the severity of symptoms decreased.
Alcohol abstinence is recommended for breast-feeding mothers.

more_examples.text: Infant-mortality rates are a reflection of numerous medical factors, including the mother's prenatal care and abstinence from drugs and cigarettes.
The study compared the success of different approaches in helping smokers achieve long-term abstinence.
Drug users reported fewer manic episodes during periods of abstinence.
He credits his long life to the healthful cooking of his wife of 50 years, and his abstinence from tobacco, alcohol, coffee and tea.
Their programs send the message that abstinence is the expected standard for teens.
Except for abstinence, latex condoms are the best protection against STDs, including herpes and AIDS.

definitions.definition: the practice of teaching people that they should not have sex outside of marriage , especially when this is taught instead of other forms of sex education such as teaching about contraception (= methods of preventing pregnancy )
definitions.def_translation: 节欲教育;禁欲教育（尤指劝人戒除婚外情，却不提供其他内容的性教育，比如避孕）

examples.text: Abstinence education teaches children and adolescents that abstaining from sexual activity is the only certain method of avoiding pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections.
examples.translation: 禁欲教育教导儿童和青少年，避免性行为是避孕和防止感染性病的唯一确定方法。

more_examples.text: The proposal stated that abstinence education should teach that "sexual activity" outside of marriage is wrong and psychologically and physically harmful.
Abstinence education has been found to be ineffective in decreasing HIV risk in the developed world.
He said that the Abstinence Education program would teach America's youth that abstinence is the most effective means of preventing pregnancy, abortion, and sexually transmitted diseases.
Since the mid-1990s abstinence education has been introduced in some UK schools.

definitions.definition: US spelling of abstinence programme
definitions.def_translation: 节欲运动;禁欲运动 （abstinence programme的美式拼法）

definitions.definition: a programme of education that teaches people that they should not have sex outside of marriage , especially when this is taught instead of other forms of sex education such as teaching about contraception (= methods of preventing pregnancy )
definitions.def_translation: 节欲运动;禁欲运动（尤指劝人戒除婚外情，却不提供其他内容的性教育，比如避孕）

examples.text: The study has been interpreted as showing that abstinence programmes are failing and that condom use should be encouraged.
examples.translation: 该研究被认为是证明了禁欲运动正在失败，应该鼓励使用安全套。

more_examples.text: Abstinence programmes were seen as a way of tackling HIV.
Abstinence programmes have been ineffective and even counter-productive, she claims.
The new administration withdrew dedicated funding for abstinence programmes.

definitions.definition: used to describe a policy or a type of education that teaches people that they should not have sex outside of marriage , and does not teach about any other methods of preventing pregnancy or disease
definitions.def_translation: 唯节欲论的（尤指劝人戒除婚外情，却不介绍其他避孕或防止性病的方法）

examples.text: At my former high school, abstinence-only education was required for all students.
examples.translation: 在我以前就读的高中，所有学生都需要接受唯节欲论的性教育。

more_examples.text: Texas has a staunch abstinence-only policy, and denies contraceptives to minors who do not have parental consent.
According to the institute, there is no evidence that abstinence-only education delays teen sexual activity.
Faith-based organizations favour abstinence-only sex education.
Christian fundamentalists generally take an "abstinence-only" approach.
The only state-funded sex education programs in the state are abstinence-only.

definitions.definition: used to describe a policy of telling people not to use drugs or alcohol at all, rather than trying to reduce the risk in some other way

examples.text: Their approach to treating people with substance use disorders is quite different from the traditional "abstinence-only" philosophy.
examples.translation: 他们治疗药物滥用失常患者的方法与传统的“唯节欲”理念截然不同。

more_examples.text: Texas has a staunch abstinence-only policy, and denies contraceptives to minors who do not have parental consent.
According to the institute, there is no evidence that abstinence-only education delays teen sexual activity.
Faith-based organizations favour abstinence-only sex education.
Christian fundamentalists generally take an "abstinence-only" approach.
The only state-funded sex education programs in the state are abstinence-only.

definitions.definition: completely avoiding something such as alcohol or sex

examples.text: sexually abstinent
examples.translation: 禁性欲的

examples.text: He has now been abstinent from alcohol for four years.
examples.translation: 到现在他戒酒四年了。

more_examples.text: I choose to be abstinent and will wait to have sex until after I am married.
He is totally abstinent at conferences because he wants to stay focused.
Unless you are completely abstinent, there is no other 100% perfect method of birth control.

definitions.definition: existing as an idea , feeling , or quality , not as a material object
definitions.def_translation: 抽象的;纯理论的;纯概念的

examples.text: Truth and beauty are abstract concepts.
examples.translation: 真和美都是抽象的概念。

definitions.definition: An abstract argument or discussion is general and not based on particular examples .
definitions.def_translation: （辩论或讨论）抽象的；空泛的；空洞的

examples.text: This debate is becoming too abstract - let's have some hard facts!
examples.translation: 这场辩论变得太空洞了，拿出一些具体的事实根据来吧！

definitions.definition: general ideas

examples.text: So far we've only discussed the question in the abstract (= without referring to any real examples).
examples.translation: 目前我们只是泛泛地讨论过这个问题。

examples.text: I have difficulty dealing with the abstract - let's discuss particular cases.
examples.translation: 我难以理解抽象概念，我们讨论一些具体的案例吧。

more_examples.text: It is sometimes easier to illustrate an abstract concept by analogy with something concrete.
He is good at explaining quite complex, abstract ideas in a nice simple way.
Your idea is rather vague and abstract - could you explain it in a bit more detail, please?
These early humans were clearly capable of abstract thought, and probably language too.
Some of these new theories are so abstract that they don't seem to relate to our everyday work at all.

definitions.definition: used to refer to a type of painting , drawing , or sculpture that uses shapes , lines , and colour in a way that does not try to represent the appearance of people or things

examples.text: abstract art
examples.translation: 抽象艺术

examples.text: an abstract painter
examples.translation: 抽象派画家

definitions.definition: a short form of a speech , article , book , etc., giving only the most important facts or ideas

examples.text: There is a section at the end of the magazine that includes abstracts of recent articles/books.
examples.translation: 杂志的最后一部分收录了近期发表的文章／出版的书籍的摘要。

definitions.definition: a painting that uses shapes , lines , and colour in a way that does not try to represent the appearance of people or things
definitions.def_translation: 抽象画;抽象派艺术作品

definitions.definition: a noun that refers to a thing that does not exist as a material object

examples.text: "Happiness", "honesty", and "liberty" are abstract nouns.
examples.translation: “幸福”、“诚实”和“自由”都是抽象名词。

definitions.definition: not giving attention to what is happening around you because you are thinking about something else
definitions.def_translation: 心不在焉的；走神的；出神的

examples.text: He gave her an abstracted glance, then returned to his book.
examples.translation: 他心不在焉地瞥了她一眼，又一头扎进他的书里。

definitions.definition: without paying attention to what is happening around you because you are thinking about something else

in physics , a machine that makes particles (= small pieces of matter ) move very fast

examples.text: Start-up accelerators have become increasingly popular elements of the regional growth infrastructure.

examples.translation: 突出每一小节的第一个音符。

examples.translation: 她的裙子衣带系得很紧，凸显出苗条的腰身。

examples.translation: 这项新政策更加突显了政府对无家可归者的扶助不足。

examples.translation: 你们接受信用卡支付吗？

examples.translation: 她赴孟买领取最新一部小说所获奖项。

examples.translation: 新型咖啡机接受任何面值的硬币。

examples.translation: 我们把这份工作给了她，但是我不知道她会不会接受。

examples.translation: 我刚刚接受了参加首映晚会的邀请。

examples.translation: 他们邀请我参加婚礼，但是我还没有决定去不去。
