definitions.definition: An accident-prone person often has accidents , usually because they are very awkward .
definitions.def_translation: （通常因为笨拙而）易出事故的;易遭意外的

definitions.definition: happening or existing by chance

examples.text: Reports suggest that eleven soldiers were killed by accidental fire from their own side.
examples.translation: 报道暗示11名士兵被己方炮火误射而丧生。

examples.text: The site was located after the accidental discovery of bones in a field.
examples.translation: 有人在田地里意外地发现遗骨后，这个遗址才被发现。

examples.text: He plays a naive salesman who becomes an accidental hero by saving a child's life.

more_examples.text: All our household goods are insured against accidental damage.
The coroner concluded that his death was accidental.
Our meeting wasn't planned - it was completely accidental.
She says she didn't mean to break it, but I don't think it was accidental.
When my condition improved after taking the herbal medicine, the doctor said it was purely accidental.

definitions.definition: a sign showing that there is a temporary change from the key signature (= the set of musical notes that should normally be played for a particular piece of music )
definitions.def_translation: 临时变音记号，临时升降号

definitions.definition: a bird that is found in a place where birds of its type are not usually found
definitions.def_translation: 出现在非通常栖息地的鸟

examples.text: You may spot accidentals driven in by the stormy weather.
examples.translation: 你可能会观察到一些鸟因为恶劣天气而被迫飞到它们通常不会出现的地方。

definitions.definition: a verdict (= an opinion stated at the end of a trial ) that is given when a death was the result of an accident and not of murder or suicide
by chance or by mistake

examples.text: I accidentally knocked a glass over.
examples.translation: 我不小心打翻了一个杯子。

definitions.definition: If you do something accidentally on purpose , you do it intentionally but pretend it happened by chance .
definitions.def_translation: 明明故意却装出无心的样子；假装不是故意地

examples.text: I've never liked these glasses of Peter's. I might drop them one day - accidentally on purpose.
examples.translation: 我从来就不喜欢彼得的这副眼镜，或许什么时候我会假装无意把它给摔了。

definitions.definition: said after an accident in order to make it seem less bad
definitions.def_translation: （事故发生后说的安慰话）出事是难免的。

definitions.definition: public approval and praise

examples.text: Despite the critical acclaim, the novel did not sell well.
examples.translation: 虽然这部小说在评论界赢得一片叫好之声，但并不畅销。

examples.text: Her first novel was published to great acclaim in 2018.
Hamlet was played by Ion Caramitrou to rapturous acclaim.
examples.translation: 罗马尼亚演员杨•卡拉米特鲁饰演的哈姆雷特获得好评如潮。

definitions.definition: to give public approval and praise

examples.text: She was widely acclaimed for her contribution to the discovery.
She is being acclaimed (= publicly recognized) as the greatest dancer of her generation.
examples.translation: 她被赞誉为同时代最伟大的舞蹈演员。

definitions.definition: attracting public approval and praise

examples.text: "Dinner Party", based on the critically acclaimed novel by Bill Davies, was made into a film last year.
examples.translation: 《晚宴》改编自比尔·戴维斯（Bill Davies）广受好评的小说，于去年被拍成电影。

examples.text: an acclaimed artist/writer/poet
examples.translation: 著名的艺术家/作家/诗人

more_examples.text: He is the author of a widely acclaimed new study on the subject.
"Billy Elliot" is the acclaimed drama about a working-class boy who dreams of becoming a ballet dancer.
Acclaimed photographer James Nachtwey spent several weeks in Sudan documenting the tragedy in Darfur.

definitions.definition: public approval and praise

examples.text: His speech was greeted with (shouts of) acclamation.
examples.translation: 他的演讲博得阵阵喝彩（声）。

definitions.definition: to change to suit different conditions of life , weather , etc., or to make someone or something do this
definitions.def_translation: （使）适应;（使）习惯于;（使）服水土（同 acclimatize）

examples.text: Teachers begin acclimating young students to new learning technologies in a simple way.
It can be difficult to acclimate to such extreme elevations.
Apparently the zoo animals had become acclimated to the crowd noise and were no longer startled by it.
examples.translation: 显然动物园中的动物已经对人群发出的噪音习以为常，不再会因此受到惊吓。

examples.text: Gradually acclimate yourself to working out in the heat.

more_examples.text: Take advantage of any pre-college orientation programs so you will able to acclimate to the campus in advance.
It can take several months for 9th graders to get acclimated to high school.
In order to acclimate my body to the new time zone, I got up early.
As soon as I signed the contract I moved to Cleveland, because I wanted to acclimate myself as soon as possible.

definitions.definition: the process of changing to suit different conditions of life , weather , etc., or the act of making someone or something do this

examples.text: Overseas drivers driving on the opposite side of the road for the first time may need a few days of acclimatisation.
examples.translation: 海外来的司机第一次在公路另一侧行驶，可能需要几天的适应期。

examples.text: Inadequate acclimatization may lead to altitude sickness above 8,000 ft.
examples.translation: 适应不足可能会导致在8000英尺以上时出现高原病。

more_examples.text: This excursion requires previous acclimatization to the altitude.
The acclimatization period was one week.
The advice and support they got from the lottery organizer contributed to their successful acclimatisation to sudden wealth.

definitions.definition: to change to suit different conditions of life , weather , etc., or to make someone or something do this

examples.text: The defending champion has acclimatized to the 30°C sunshine by spending the past month in Florida.
examples.translation: 卫冕冠军上个月在佛罗里达呆了整整一个月，已经适应了90华氏度的曝晒。

examples.text: More time will be needed for the troops and equipment to become acclimatised to desert conditions.
examples.translation: 军队和装备需要更多的时间来适应沙漠环境。

examples.text: "Why is it that it rains all the time in England?" "Don't worry - you'll soon acclimatise."
examples.translation: “英格兰怎么老下雨？”“别担心，你很快就会适应的。”

examples.text: We found it impossible to acclimatize ourselves to the new working conditions.
examples.translation: 我们发现自己无法适应新的工作环境。

definitions.definition: an upward slope ; the fact of sloping upward

examples.text: The village was in a vale between two gentle acclivities.
examples.translation: 这个小村庄处于两个上行缓坡之间的山谷中。

more_examples.text: I left the wooded valley and proceeded to mount the steep acclivity of Wildfell.
This mountain looks a monster, its very steep acclivities soaring skyward in terraces of uncompromising cliffs.
Behind the church, and sloping up a gentle acclivity, was its capacious burying-ground.
He encompassed the city with a wall, and made use of the acclivity of the place for making its fortifications stronger.

definitions.definition: praise and approval

examples.text: She has sold millions of records and earned numerous awards and accolades over a 30-year career.
Her approval was the highest accolade he could receive.
examples.translation: 她的嘉许就是他所能得到的最高赞赏。

examples.text: He's been granted the ultimate accolade - his face on a postage stamp.
examples.translation: 他获得了最高荣誉——他的头像被印在了邮票上。

definitions.definition: to provide with a place to live or to be stored in
definitions.def_translation: 为…提供住宿;容纳;为…提供空间

examples.text: New students may be accommodated in halls of residence.
examples.translation: 新生可以住在学校宿舍楼里。

examples.text: There wasn't enough space to accommodate the files.
examples.translation: 没有足够的空间存放这些档案。

more_examples.text: While he was at the library, Steve decided to seek out some information on accommodation in the area.
Feeling guilty for the homeless is one thing, finding cheap secure accommodation for them is quite another thing.
Hostels are usually provided as a stopgap until the families can be housed in permanent accommodation.
There's accommodation for about five hundred students on campus.
The price includes travel and accommodation but meals are extra.

definitions.definition: to give what is needed to someone
definitions.def_translation: 为…提供方便;对…予以照顾性考虑

examples.text: We always try to accommodate (= help) our clients with financial assistance if necessary.
examples.translation: 必要时，我们总是尽力为客户提供财务上的帮助。

examples.text: The new policies fail to accommodate people with disabilities.
examples.translation: 新政策未能满足残障人士的需求。

definitions.definition: to change yourself or your behaviour to suit another person or new conditions

examples.text: Some find it hard to accommodate themselves to the new working conditions.
examples.translation: 有些人觉得很难适应新的工作环境。

examples.text: She was desperately trying to accommodate herself to her new living arrangements.
At that point, I had not accommodated myself to the life of a fisherman.
We tried to find a way of accommodating ourselves to a society we disliked.
As a politician, he had to be able to accommodate himself to public opinion.

definitions.definition: (of an eye ) to change the shape of the lens in order to focus (= see clearly )
definitions.def_translation: （眼睛）调节晶状体形状实现聚焦

definitions.definition: used to describe a person who is eager or willing to help other people , for example by changing his or her plans
definitions.def_translation: 乐于助人的;与人方便的;通融的

examples.text: I'm sure she'll help you - she's always very accommodating.
examples.translation: 我相信她肯定会帮助你的——她一向乐于助人。

definitions.definition: a place to stay or live

examples.text: They paid for his flights and hotel accommodation.
examples.translation: 他们支付了他的机票和酒店住宿。

examples.text: There's a shortage of cheap accommodation in the city.
There is accommodation for about five hundred students on campus.
Hostels are a temporary solution until the families can be housed in permanent accommodation.

more_examples.text: While he was at the library, Steve decided to seek out some information on accommodation in the area.
The price includes travel and accommodation but meals are extra.
Feeling guilty about the homeless is relatively easy; finding cheap, secure accommodation for them is more difficult.

definitions.definition: an agreement between two groups who have different opinions on a subject , or the process of reaching an agreement like this

examples.text: She may be able to reach an accommodation with other EU members on the question of immigration.
examples.translation: 她也许可在移民问题上与其他欧盟成员国达成协议。

examples.text: He sought accommodation with the United States.

definitions.definition: a special arrangement that is made for a person or group that has different needs to others
definitions.def_translation: 特殊安排|特殊措施|特殊调整

examples.text: The hotel tries to make accommodations for people with small children.
Companies should make reasonable accommodations for disabled employees.
As a host, what do you consider to be a reasonable accommodation for someone with a medically restricted diet?
As a business we offer flexible work hours and other accommodations for parents.
My children had no recognized disability so I did not qualify for any accommodation with regard to work hours.

more_examples.text: I think we could have come to an accommodation about a reasonable use of the site, but the other side refused to negotiate.
He believed that the Empire should be ruled through accommodations with local people.
We must address the issue of accommodations for gifted students.
Some accommodations were allowed for students with learning difficulties.
Accommodations were made for people with particular religious practices.

definitions.definition: the process by which an eye is able to focus (= see clearly ) by changing the shape of the lens
definitions.def_translation: （眼睛）调节晶状体形状实现聚焦

definitions.definition: a place to stay when you are travelling , especially a hotel room

examples.text: Sweepstakes winners will enjoy a week-long stay in luxury accommodations in Las Vegas.
examples.translation: 赌金全赢制赌博的中奖人可以在拉斯韦加斯的豪华旅馆里高高兴兴住上一周。

definitions.definition: intended to encourage economic growth by reducing interest rates (= the amount charged when people borrow money )

examples.text: He proposes to adopt a cautiously accommodative monetary policy.
examples.translation: 他建议采取谨慎降息的货币政策。

examples.text: She believed that interest rates were too accommodative.

more_examples.text: Today’s increase is modest and still leaves rates at very accommodative levels.
Global financial conditions remain accommodative, not restrictive.

definitions.definition: relating to the way that the eyes adjust (= move and change ) in order to focus (= see clearly )

examples.text: Patients undergoing cataract surgery can be fitted with accommodative intraocular lenses.
examples.translation: 接受白内障手术手术的病人可以配备可植入调节性眼内晶状体。

examples.text: The study looked at the effects of acute accommodative and pupillary dysfunction.

definitions.definition: music that is played with someone who is singing or playing the main tune

examples.text: a song with piano accompaniment
examples.translation: 由钢琴伴奏的歌曲

definitions.definition: something that you eat or drink with something else

examples.text: A dry champagne makes the ideal accompaniment to this dish.
examples.translation: 吃这道菜时，一杯干型香槟是理想的佐餐酒。

examples.text: Apple sauce is a traditional accompaniment for pork chops.

definitions.definition: someone who plays an instrument such as the piano or guitar while someone else sings or plays the main tune

examples.text: The singer's accompanist on the piano was Charles Harman.
examples.translation: 为演唱者钢琴伴奏的是查尔斯•哈曼。

definitions.definition: to go with someone or to be provided or exist at the same time as something
definitions.def_translation: 陪同，陪伴;伴随，和…一起发生（或存在）

examples.text: The course books are accompanied by four CDs.
examples.translation: 这些课本配有4张光盘。

examples.text: Depression is almost always accompanied by insomnia.
examples.translation: 抑郁症几乎总是伴有失眠。

examples.text: The salmon was accompanied by (= served with) a fresh green salad.
examples.translation: 那道三文鱼菜佐以新鲜的蔬菜色拉。

definitions.definition: to show someone how to get to somewhere

examples.text: Would you like me to accompany you to your room?
examples.translation: 我送你到房间去，好吗？

definitions.definition: to go with someone to a social event or to an entertainment
definitions.def_translation: 陪同，陪伴（某人参加社交或文娱活动）

examples.text: "May I accompany you to the ball?" he asked her.
examples.translation: “我可以陪您去参加舞会吗？”他问她。

examples.text: I have two tickets for the theatre on Saturday evening - would you like to accompany me?
examples.translation: “我有两张周六晚上的戏票，你愿意陪我一起去吗？”

more_examples.text: There's a workbook to accompany the course book.
Visitors must be accompanied by club members.
His faithful old dog accompanied him everywhere he went.
The prince is always accompanied by his bodyguards.
The school rules state that no child shall be allowed out of the school during the day, unless accompanied by an adult.

definitions.definition: to sing or play an instrument with another musician or singer

examples.text: Miss Jessop accompanied Mr Bentley on the piano.
examples.translation: 杰索普小姐为本特利先生钢琴伴奏。

examples.text: Erin sang while I accompanied on the guitar.

definitions.definition: appearing or going with someone or something else
definitions.def_translation: 伴随的，陪伴的；和…一起发生（或存在）的

examples.text: Front-page stories broke the news of the star leaving, and accompanying photographs showed her getting on the plane.
examples.translation: 报纸头版爆出明星离开的消息，同时配有她登机而去的照片。

examples.text: Children under twelve require an accompanying parent or guardian to see this movie.
examples.translation: 12岁以下的儿童看这部电影必须要有父母或监护人的陪同。

definitions.definition: a person who helps someone else to commit a crime or to do something morally wrong
to finish something successfully or to achieve something

examples.text: The students accomplished the task in less than ten minutes.
examples.translation: 学生们不到10分钟就完成了任务。

examples.text: She accomplished such a lot during her visit.
examples.translation: 她在访问期间取得了丰硕的成果。

examples.text: I feel as if I've accomplished nothing since I left my job.
examples.translation: 我觉得辞掉工作以后就一直在虚度光阴。

more_examples.text: You can actually accomplish a lot more by gentle persuasion.
If you are fit, the climb can be accomplished in less than three hours.
He believes you can accomplish a lot in a relatively short space of time.
New technology means that astronomers can accomplish in a single night what once took years.
The new coach told the press that he believed his team could accomplish great things.

definitions.definition: skilled
definitions.def_translation: 熟练的；有造诣的；有才艺的

examples.text: She's a very accomplished pianist/painter/horsewoman.
examples.translation: 她是一位很有造诣的钢琴家／很有才华的画家／技艺高超的骑师。

examples.text: He was accomplished in all the arts.
examples.translation: 他精通各门艺术。

definitions.definition: something that is successful , or that is achieved after a lot of work or effort

examples.text: Getting the two leaders to sign a peace treaty was his greatest accomplishment.
examples.translation: 他最大的成就是促成了两位领导人签署和平协议。

definitions.definition: the finishing of something

examples.text: We celebrated the successful accomplishment of our task.
examples.translation: 我们庆祝圆满完成任务。

definitions.definition: a skill

examples.text: Cordon bleu cookery is just one of her many accomplishments.
examples.translation: 她多才多艺，创办蓝带厨艺学校仅是其中之一。

definitions.definition: (a formal ) agreement

examples.text: On 31 May the two leaders signed a peace accord.
examples.translation: 5月31日两位领导人签署了一项和平协议。

examples.text: The project is completely in accord with government policy.
examples.translation: 该项目完全符合政府政策。

examples.text: A vague murmur of accord rose from around the table.
UKBefore 1987, the accord between the Labour government and the unions was a simple affair.
examples.translation: 1987年以前，工党政府和工会之间很容易达成一致。

more_examples.text: An international accord banning land mines was signed in Canada last month.
The accord ended nearly two decades of civil war in the region.
Ministers from 20 countries approved an accord to cooperate in the fight against terrorism.
Diplomats worked through the night in an attempt to forge an accord that would resolve the crisis.

definitions.definition: If you do something of your own accord, you do it without being asked to do it:

examples.text: She came of her own accord. No one asked her to come.
examples.translation: 她自愿来的，没有人让她来。

definitions.definition: If people do something with one accord, they do it together and in complete agreement :

examples.text: With one accord, the delegates walked out of the conference.
examples.translation: 所有代表一致退出会议。

definitions.definition: to treat someone specially , usually by showing respect
definitions.def_translation: （通常指恭敬地）给予（特殊待遇）;授予

examples.text: The massed crowds of supporters accorded him a hero's welcome.
examples.translation: 蜂拥云集的支持者们给予他英雄般的欢迎。

examples.text: Certainly in our society teachers don't enjoy the respect that is accorded to doctors and lawyers.
examples.translation: 的确，在我们这个社会中，老师没有得到像医生和律师所受到的那种尊敬。

definitions.definition: to be the same as something, or to agree with something

examples.text: His version of events does not accord with witnesses' statements.
examples.translation: 他对事件的说法和目击者们的陈述不一致。

definitions.definition: following or obeying a rule , law , wish , etc.

examples.text: In accordance with her wishes, she was buried in France.
examples.translation: 按照她的遗愿，人们将她安葬在法国。

definitions.definition: as stated by

examples.text: According to Sarah they're not getting on very well at the moment.
examples.translation: 据萨拉说，他们目前关系不是太好。

examples.text: According to our records you owe us $130.
examples.translation: 根据我们的记录，你欠我们130美元。

more_examples.text: An agreement is looking decidedly difficult according to the newspapers.
the Gospel according to St Mark
According to Ella, it was the first time they had met.
According to these documents, you still owe us £2,000.
You've been very rude, according to your mother.

definitions.definition: in a way that agrees with

examples.text: Students are all put in different groups according to their ability.
examples.translation: 所有的学生都按能力进行编组。

definitions.definition: Something that happens according to plan happens in the way it was intended to:

examples.text: Did it all go according to plan?
examples.translation: 一切都是按计划进行的吗？

more_examples.text: The books in the library are classified by/according to subject.
Vegetable prices fluctuate according to the season.
The books are graded according to the difficulty of the language.
I grouped the children according to age.
The books were organized on the shelves according to their size.

definitions.definition: Something that happens according to plan happens in the way it was intended to.
definitions.def_translation: 按部就班;按照计划进行

examples.text: Did it all go according to plan?
examples.translation: 一切都是按计划进行的吗？

examples.text: If everything goes according to plan, the building work will be finished by summer.
Officials said the entire event had gone according to plan.
The journey went according to plan and we arrived before eight.
It wasn't a surprise - that was all according to plan.

definitions.definition: in a way that is suitable or right for the situation

examples.text: When we receive your instructions we will act accordingly.
examples.translation: 我们接到你的指令就会遵命行事。

examples.text: She's an expert in her field, and is paid accordingly.
examples.translation: 她是这一领域的专家，且得到了相应的报酬。

definitions.definition: a box-shaped musical instrument consisting of a folded central part with a keyboard , played by pushing the two ends towards each other
to go up to or stop and speak to someone in a threatening way
definitions.def_translation: （贸然）上前搭讪;（唐突地）走近谈话

examples.text: I'm usually accosted by beggars and drunks as I walk to the station.
examples.translation: 去车站的路上，经常有乞丐和酒鬼上前跟我搭讪。

definitions.definition: an arrangement with a bank to keep your money there and to allow you to take it out when you need to

examples.text: I withdrew my money and asked the bank to close my account.
I've opened an account with a building society .
examples.translation: 我在房屋互助协会开了个账户。

examples.text: I paid the money into my account this morning.
examples.translation: 今天上午我把钱存入了我的账户。

examples.text: UKShe paid the cheque into her account.
examples.translation: 她把支票存入了账户。

examples.text: USShe deposited the check in/into her account.
examples.translation: 她把支票存入了账户。

examples.text: I need to withdraw some money from my account.
examples.translation: 我得从我的账户上取出一些钱来。

more_examples.text: I was relieved to see from my statement that my account was in credit.
I closed that bank account when I came to London.
The account was in debit at the end of the month.
To open an account, you need to make a minimum deposit of $500.
Alison drew some money out of her account to pay for our trip.

definitions.definition: a written or spoken description or record of an event

examples.text: She gave a thrilling account of her life in the jungle.
examples.translation: 她把自己在丛林中生活的经历描述得惊险刺激。

examples.text: He kept a detailed account of the suspect's movements.
examples.translation: 他详细记录了犯罪嫌疑人的一举一动。

examples.text: Several eyewitnesses' accounts differed considerably from the official version of events.
examples.translation: 几个目击者对于事件的叙述和官方的说法有很大出入。

definitions.definition: as said by most people :

examples.text: By all accounts, San Francisco is a city that's easy to fall in love with.
examples.translation: 人人都说旧金山是个很容易令人倾心的城市。

definitions.definition: If something is true by your own account, what you say is true although you have not proved it:

examples.text: By his own account, he's quite wealthy.
examples.translation: 他自称很富有。

more_examples.text: She gave a clear, factual account of the attack.
The book is a work of fiction and not intended as a historical account.
The foregoing account was written 50 years after the incident.
She gave a hair-raising account of her escape through the desert.
She gave a clear and lucid account of her plans for the company's future.

definitions.definition: because of something:

examples.text: He doesn't drink alcohol on account of his poor health.
examples.translation: 出于健康原因，他不喝酒。

definitions.definition: an agreement with a shop or business that allows you to buy things and pay for them later

examples.text: Could you put it on/charge it to my account (= can I pay for it later), please?
examples.translation: 把这笔钱记在我的（赊购）账上好吗？

examples.text: Do you have an account at this store/with us, madam?
examples.translation: 女士，你在我们商店有赊购账户吗？

examples.text: Could you please settle your account in full (= give us all the money you owe us)?
examples.translation: 您可以把赊的账全结清吗？

definitions.definition: a customer who does business with a company

examples.text: If the advertising agency loses this account, it will make a big dent in their profits.
examples.translation: 如果该广告公司丢掉了这个客户，他们的利润就会锐减。

definitions.definition: to not be important :

examples.text: It's of no account to me whether he comes or not.
examples.translation: 他来不来对我来说都无关紧要。

definitions.definition: to think of someone or something in the stated way

examples.text: She was accounted a genius by all who knew her work.
examples.translation: 所有知道她作品的人都认为她是个天才。

definitions.definition: to explain the reason for something or the cause of something
definitions.def_translation: （对某人）就…作出解释;（对某人）就…作出说明

examples.text: Can you account for your absence last Friday?
examples.translation: 你能解释一下上周五你为什么缺勤吗？

examples.text: She was unable to account for over $5,000 (= she could not explain where the money was).
examples.translation: 她无法对5000多美元的去向作出解释。

examples.text: He has to account to his manager for (= tell his manager about and explain) all his movements.
examples.translation: 他不得不向经理交代清楚他的一切行动。

more_examples.text: There is £50 missing from the till - how do account for that?

definitions.definition: to form the total of something

examples.text: Students account for the vast majority of our customers.
examples.translation: 我们的顾客绝大多数是学生。

definitions.definition: the fact of being responsible for what you do and able to give a satisfactory reason for it, or the degree to which this happens

examples.text: There were furious demands for greater police accountability.
examples.translation: 人们强烈要求加强对警察的问责。

examples.text: Accountability is important these days, and managers aren't always willing to adopt risky strategies.
examples.translation: 如今，问责很重要，管理者并不总是愿意采取高风险的策略。

more_examples.text: Citizens must demand accountability from their leaders.

definitions.definition: Someone who is accountable is completely responsible for what they do and must be able to give a satisfactory reason for it.
definitions.def_translation: 应负责任的；应作解释的；应加以说明的

examples.text: She is accountable only to the managing director.
examples.translation: 她只对总裁负责。

examples.text: Politicians should be accountable to the public who elected them.
examples.translation: 政界人士应对他们的选民负责。

examples.text: The recent tax reforms have made government more accountable for its spending.
examples.translation: 最近的税务改革使政府的开支更加透明化。

examples.text: You have to hold your employees accountable for their actions, or else they will just do whatever they please.

definitions.definition: the job of being an accountant

examples.translation: 他的职业是会计。

examples.text: an accountancy firm
examples.translation: 会计师事务所

examples.translation: 会计师事务所

the job of being an accountant
an official record of all the money a person or company has spent and received

examples.translation: 该代理处没有得到菲律宾领事馆的批准，无权向国外的菲律宾人提供承包合同。

examples.translation: 该学院于1965年获得完全的官方认证。

definitions.definition: officially recognized or approved

definitions.definition: to gradually increase or grow by the addition of new layers or parts , or to cause something to do this

examples.text: Eventually, the material accretes by gravity to form separate planets.
examples.translation: 最终，通过重力吸积的物质形成了独立的星球。

examples.translation: 科学家在湖面堆积形成的冰层上往下钻探了两英里。

examples.translation: 由于新股东的逐渐加入，资金增加了。

examples.translation: 房间多年没有打扫，积了厚厚的灰尘。

examples.translation: 新的道路修建计划几乎不会给该城市带来什么利益。

examples.translation: 拉美人是如何适应美国的生活的？

definitions.definition: the process of changing so that you become more like people from a different culture , or of making someone change in this way

examples.translation: 电子游戏的问题在于它们会使人上瘾。

examples.translation: 这种人造黄油里面都是添加剂——看看标签说明就知道了！

examples.translation: 恐怕我是被太阳晒糊涂了，我听不懂这些指示。

examples.translation: 他向观众说了几句开场白。

examples.translation: 将链接粘贴到地址栏可查看图片。

examples.translation: 当页面加载时，地址栏包含一个复杂的 URL。

examples.translation: 他用略带鼻音的声音唱歌。

examples.translation: 我没有充足的时间来准备。

definitions.definition: a word that describes a noun or pronoun

examples.text: "Big", "boring", "purple", and "obvious" are all adjectives.
examples.translation: “大的”、“无聊的”、“紫色的”以及“明显的”这些词都是形容词。

definitions.definition: to be very near, next to, or touching

examples.translation: 马厩紧挨着房子的西厢。

examples.translation: 这儿正是这三个街区的交界点。

definitions.definition: near, next to, or touching

examples.translation: 我们要了相邻的房间。

definitions.definition: to have a pause or rest during a formal meeting or trial

examples.translation: 休会至星期二。

examples.translation: 我们暂停先去吃午饭好吗？

examples.translation: 我们到客厅喝杯咖啡好吗？

examples.translation: 辩护律师要求休庭。

definitions.definition: to announce a decision or consider something, especially officially
definitions.def_translation: （尤指正式地）判决，宣判，裁决;认为

examples.translation: 比赛进行到半小时时，佩特森被判对杰克逊犯规而被罚下场。

examples.translation: 人们请他来对这场争端作出裁定。

examples.translation: 他被请来裁决一起当地的土地纠纷。

examples.translation: 布莱克被裁定赢得比赛。

definitions.definition: the act of judging a case , competition , or argument , or of making a formal decision about something

examples.translation: 交易的合法性仍在法庭上有待裁决（=正在决定）。

examples.translation: 他的判决后来被发现是错误的。

examples.translation: 比赛的评判由学院负责。

definitions.definition: a person or group that makes an official decision about something, especially about who is right in a disagreement

examples.translation: 她担任了这场争端的裁定人。

definitions.definition: something added or connected to a larger or more important thing

examples.translation: 法官要求他据实回答。

examples.translation: 如果椅子太高了，你可以把它调到适合你的高度。

examples.translation: 作为一名老师，你必须调整教学方法来适应那些学得较慢的孩子的需要。

examples.translation: 她整了整裙子，深吸一口气，走进了房间。

examples.translation: 我不习惯独自生活。

examples.translation: 她的眼睛慢慢适应了黑暗。

examples.translation: 她稍微调了调相机的焦距。

definitions.definition: the ability to become more familiar with a new situation

examples.translation: 他到现在还没有适应从学生生活到工作的变化。

examples.translation: 适应障碍的许多症状跟重度抑郁症相似。

examples.translation: 参与这项研究的所有女性都接受了采用它莫西芬的辅助治疗。

examples.translation: 我觉得在和他的交往中该采用一种不同的策略了。

examples.translation: 征收新税将迫使公司采取节能措施。

examples.translation: 狂犬病人中有50%会出现恐水症和气流恐惧症的情况。

definitions.definition: any musical instrument in which sound is produced mainly by the vibration (= continuous quick movement ) of air

examples.text: The category of aerophones includes wind instruments, accordions, and whirly tubes.
examples.translation: 管乐器包括吹奏乐器、手风琴和音鸣管等。

more_examples.text: If instruments are to be classified, the more inclusive terms idiophone, membranophone, aerophone and chordophone should replace strings, brass, woodwinds and percussion.
Aerophones form one of the main categories of instruments in the standard classification of Hornbostel and Sachs (1914).
Keyboards are integral to many aerophones (eg the accordion), chordophones (eg the piano), and electrophones (eg the synthesizer).
The sound in an aerophone instrument may be produced by reed vibration.

definitions.definition: a vehicle designed for air travel that has wings and one or more engines

examples.text: She has her own private aeroplane.
examples.translation: 她拥有私人飞机。

more_examples.text: I've nearly finished making my model aeroplane - I just have to glue the wings on.
The aeroplane had to make a forced landing because one of the engines cut out.
To be honest, the thought of jumping out of a moving aeroplane makes my hair stand on end.
Anything to do with aeroplanes and flying fascinates him.
Model aeroplanes come in pieces which you have to put together.

definitions.definition: → airplane mode
a metal container in which liquids are kept under pressure and forced out in a spray

examples.text: He's seen fires started by aerosols being sprayed on electrical equipment.
Aerosol cans are banned from aircraft cabins.

more_examples.text: More babies suffered diarrhoea in homes where air fresheners - including sticks, sprays and aerosols - were used daily.
Finish by misting your curls with an aerosol hair spray.
As well as helping clouds form, aerosols absorb or scatter sunlight.
An aerosol can travel considerable distances downwind, and still remain infectious to people.

definitions.definition: a mixture of particles (= extremely small pieces of matter ) and the liquid or gas that they are contained in, that can spread through the air

examples.text: The virus is spread primarily by aerosols, so that could be by sneezing, coughing, or even talking.
Aerosols are one type of air pollution - the tiny particles suspended everywhere in our atmosphere.

definitions.definition: to turn or be turned into an aerosol (= a mixture of extremely small pieces of matter and the liquid or gas that they are contained in, that can spread through the air )

examples.text: Evidence suggests that the coronavirus can aerosolize only under very limited conditions.
examples.translation: 证据显示冠状病毒只有在非常有限的条件下才会成为气溶胶。

examples.text: The study suggests the virus is aerosolized through talking and exhalation.
examples.translation: 这一研究提示病毒在交谈和呼气过程中成为气溶胶。

more_examples.text: Any tool that will aerosolize bacteria into an invisible cloud could be used to weaponize anthrax.
The research found no aerosolized coronavirus particles in the hospital rooms of Covid-19 patients.
The biological weapons programs of the United States and the Soviet Union developed techniques to aerosolize plague directly, eliminating dependence on the unpredictable flea vector.
I don't think he ever intended to kill anybody. He probably had no clue that the agent would aerosolize through envelopes and kill postal workers.

definitions.definition: producing or operating aircraft or spacecraft
definitions.def_translation: 航空航天工业的;航空航天器制造的

examples.text: the aerospace industry
examples.translation: 航空航天工业

examples.text: an aerospace company
examples.translation: 航空航天技术公司

definitions.definition: an aircraft such as a hot-air balloon or an airship , that rises off the ground using a gas that is lighter than air
a city that has an airport at its centre and has developed around it
definitions.def_translation: （以机场为中心发展起来的）航空城，空港商业城，空港都市区

examples.text: They hope to make the region a global transportation center, creating an aerotropolis.
examples.translation: 他们希望将这个地区发展成一个交通中心，创建一座空港商业城。

definitions.definition: a person who understands and enjoys beauty

examples.text: The ugliness of the city would make an aesthete like you shudder.
examples.translation: 这座城市之丑陋会使你这样的唯美主义者不寒而栗。

definitions.definition: relating to the enjoyment or study of beauty

examples.text: The new building has little aesthetic value/appeal.
examples.translation: 新楼几乎没有什么美学价值。

definitions.definition: An aesthetic object or a work of art is one that shows great beauty .

examples.text: furniture that is both aesthetic and functional
examples.translation: 既美观又实用的家具

definitions.definition: in a way that relates to the enjoyment or study of beauty

examples.text: I like objects to be both functional and aesthetically pleasing.
examples.translation: 我喜欢既实用又美观的物品。

examples.text: The three artists have very little in common aesthetically.
examples.translation: 从美学的角度上看，这三位艺术家几乎没有共同之处。

more_examples.text: A hedge is a durable, less expensive, and often more aesthetically satisfying alternative to fencing.
I would love to live in a well-designed, aesthetically pleasing, eco-friendly house.
He's one of the best directors in Japan at coming up with aesthetically interesting uses of CGI.
The purpose of the archive is to ensure that historically or aesthetically important recordings are preserved for future generations.
It is an aesthetically beautiful film with gorgeous cinematography.

definitions.definition: in a beautiful or artistic way

examples.text: The table has various objects arranged aesthetically on it.
examples.translation: 桌子上的各种物品的摆放很有美感。

more_examples.text: A hedge is a durable, less expensive, and often more aesthetically satisfying alternative to fencing.
I would love to live in a well-designed, aesthetically pleasing, eco-friendly house.

The purpose of the archive is to ensure that historically or aesthetically important recordings are preserved for future generations.
It is an aesthetically beautiful film with gorgeous cinematography.

definitions.definition: a trained person whose job is to improve the appearance and health of a customer's skin

examples.text: She gets a facial every two weeks from a well-known aesthetician.
examples.translation: 她每两周接受一次知名美容师的面部护理。

examples.text: The centre's aestheticians offer treatments such as micro peels, which can help with age spots and sun spots.
examples.translation: 该中心的美容师提供微换肤等治疗方法，可以帮助消除老年斑和晒斑。

more_examples.text: Our members are all skincare specialists, both nurses and aestheticians.
An aesthetician inserts a sterile needle that emits a low-level electrical current into the hair follicle, killing it so it won't produce any more hair.
Sally is a licensed aesthetician and massage therapist.

definitions.definition: abbreviation for after extra time : used when giving the result of a football game to show that play continued after the usual time allowed had ended , because neither team had won during that time

examples.text: Liverpool 2 Chelsea 1 (aet : 1-1 after 90 minutes)
examples.translation: 利物浦 2：切尔西 1（加时赛，90分钟1：1）

examples.text: Holland 0 Italy 0 aet: Italy win 3-1 on penalties.
examples.translation: 荷兰 0：意大利0（加时赛，点球意大利3：1胜）

more_examples.text: Aston Villa 0 - Bolton Wanderers 0 ( aet; Villa win 4-1 on penalties)
France 2 Italy 1 (aet, France win on golden goal; 1-1 after 90min)
Final: Defeated Milan on penalties (3-3 aet)

definitions.definition: the study of the causes of a disease
definitions.def_translation: 病因学（研究疾病成因的学科）

definitions.definition: written abbreviation for as fuck : used, for example on social media and in text messages , for emphasizing something
definitions.def_translation: 真他妈的（as fuck的缩写，用作强调，多用于社交媒体或手机短信等）

examples.text: He can be dumb AF sometimes.
examples.translation: 他有时候真他妈的傻。

examples.text: They're rich af.
examples.translation: 他们真他妈的有钱。

more_examples.text: This is stupid AF.
The pains were bad AF last night.
Here's how to make yourself feel better when you're as sad AF.

definitions.definition: abbreviation for assigned female at birth : used to describe a person who is or was thought to be female based on their body at their birth
definitions.def_translation: （assigned female at birth的缩写）出生时的指派性别是女性

examples.text: They wrote about their experience as a non-binary AFAB person.
examples.translation: 这些人自述经历：出生时指派性别为女性，但却不认同二元性别的区分。

examples.text: The policy states that all AFAB people are eligible to participate regardless of gender identity.
examples.translation: 该政策规定，无论性别认同为何，所有出生时指派性别为女性者都有资格参与。

examples.text: They are AFAB, but they are decidedly uninterested in identifying with a particular gender.
examples.translation: 他们出生时的指派性别是女性，但他们显然对认同特定性别不感兴趣。

more_examples.text: Not all AFAB trans people will choose to take testosterone, but many will.
I'm an AFAB non-binary lesbian.
People felt that her comments invalidated the identity of AFAB trans people.
The local drag scene has become more accepting of AFAB performers.

definitions.definition: written abbreviation for as far as I know : used when you believe that something is true , but you are not completely certain
definitions.def_translation: 据我所知（as far as I know的缩写）

definitions.definition: from or at a great distance

examples.text: People came from afar to see the show.
examples.translation: 人们从很远的地方赶来观看表演。

examples.text: I've never actually spoken to him - I've just admired him from afar.
examples.translation: 我从来没有跟他说过话——我只是“敬而远之”。

definitions.definition: abbreviation for Asian Football Confederation: the national organization for football in Asia
definitions.def_translation: 亚洲足球联盟（Asian Football Confederation的缩写）

definitions.definition: abbreviation for Aid to Families with Dependent Children: a US government programme that provides money to poor families with children
definitions.def_translation: 抚养未成年子女家庭补助计划（美国政府对有未成年子女的贫困家庭提供的补助计划，Aid to Families with Dependent Children的缩写）

definitions.definition: the quality of being friendly and easy to talk to

examples.text: Her decisiveness and affability were valuable assets.
examples.translation: 她的果断和亲和力是宝贵的财富。

examples.text: The actor uses his affability to his advantage without ever overplaying it.
examples.translation: 这位演员充分利用了他的亲和力，但没有过度发挥。

more_examples.text: She dazzled the guests with a splendid display of charm and affability.
Some of the younger staff thought their new boss lacked the easy affability of his predecessor.
The affability of the ship's captain has made this a favourite cruise.

definitions.definition: friendly and easy to talk to
definitions.def_translation: 和蔼可亲的;友善的;容易交谈的

examples.text: He struck me as an affable sort of a man.
examples.translation: 在我印象中他属于那种友善类型的人。

examples.text: She was quite affable at the meeting.
examples.translation: 会见中，她非常和蔼可亲。

definitions.definition: in a friendly way

examples.text: He greeted us affably.
examples.translation: 他亲切地和我们打招呼。

examples.text: We chatted affably for a few minutes.
examples.translation: 我们友好地聊了几分钟。

more_examples.text: The two men looked up from their game of backgammon and nodded affably.
She has always been affably articulate.
When I entered the office she smiled affably and invited me to sit.

definitions.definition: a situation or subject that is being dealt with or considered

examples.text: As a leader, he's been criticized for his inexperience in foreign affairs.
He's always interfering in (= trying to influence) other people's affairs.
She organizes her financial affairs very efficiently.
examples.translation: 她把自己的财务处理得井井有条、又快又好。

examples.text: What I do in my spare time is my affair (= only involves me).
examples.translation: 我在业余时间做什么，这是我自己的事。

definitions.definition: a matter or situation that causes strong public feeling , usually of moral disapproval
definitions.def_translation: （通常指在道德上被谴责的）事件

examples.text: The arms-dealing affair has severely damaged the reputation of the government.
examples.translation: 武器交易事件严重损害了政府的声誉。

examples.text: The president's handling of the affair has been criticized.
examples.translation: 总统对这一事件的处理遭到了抨击。

more_examples.text: The whole affair does not reflect well on the government.
He put his affairs in order before he went into hospital.
I've never been very money-minded - I leave all my business affairs to my financial adviser.
The director has come in for a lot of criticism over his handling of the affair.

definitions.definition: a sexual relationship , especially a secret one
definitions.def_translation: （尤指秘密的）性关系；私通；风流韵事

examples.text: She discovered that her husband was having an extramarital affair.
She's having an affair with a married man.
examples.translation: 她和一个有妇之夫私通。

examples.text: The book doesn't make any mention of his love affairs.
examples.translation: 这本书没有提及他的种种风流韵事。

more_examples.text: She discovered (that) her husband was having an affair.
They have been rather indiscreet about their affair.
It's an open secret around the office that they're having an affair.
Their love affair began against a backdrop of war.
She hired a private detective to find out if her husband was having an affair.

definitions.definition: an event

examples.text: The party turned out to be a quiet affair.
examples.translation: 结果聚会办得冷冷清清。

definitions.definition: an object of the type stated

examples.text: She wore a long black velvet affair.
examples.translation: 她身穿一件那种黑色天鹅绒的长裙。

definitions.definition: important government matters
to have an influence on someone or something, or to cause a change in someone or something

examples.text: Both buildings were badly affected by the fire.
examples.translation: 两座楼都在大火中严重受损。

examples.text: The divorce affected every aspect of her life.
examples.translation: 离婚使她生活的各个方面都受到了影响。

examples.text: It's a disease that affects mainly older people.
examples.translation: 这是一种主要侵扰老年人的疾病。

examples.text: I was deeply affected by the film (= it caused strong feelings in me).
examples.translation: 我被电影深深地打动了。

more_examples.text: The new rates will affect all consumers including businesses.
Researchers are looking at how a mother's health can affect the baby in the womb.
His illness affects almost every aspect of his life.
Farmers and market gardeners have been badly affected by the drought.
You couldn't fail to be affected by the film.

definitions.definition: to pretend to feel or think something

examples.text: To all his problems she affected indifference.
examples.translation: 对他所有的问题，她都装作漠不关心的样子。

definitions.definition: to start to wear or do something in order to make people admire or respect you
definitions.def_translation: （为引人注意或自抬身价而）刻意穿戴，故作

examples.text: At university he affected an upper-class accent.
examples.translation: 在大学里他拿腔捏调假装上流社会口音。

examples.text: He's recently affected a hat and cane.
examples.translation: 近来，他头上戴了顶帽子，手上拿了根拐杖，装腔作势起来。

definitions.definition: behaviour or speech that is not sincere
definitions.def_translation: 矫揉造作，做作，装模作样;假装

examples.text: She has so many little affectations.
examples.translation: 她身上有好多矫揉造作的小毛病。

examples.text: His manner reeks of affectation.
examples.translation: 他的举止做作至极。

examples.text: "It doesn't concern me," he said with an affectation of nonchalance.
examples.translation: “这不关我的事，”他故作冷漠地说。

definitions.definition: artificial and not sincere
definitions.def_translation: 矫揉造作的，做作的，装模作样的;不自然的

examples.text: an affected manner/style of writing
examples.translation: 矫揉造作的行为/文风

examples.text: I found her very affected.
examples.translation: 我觉得她非常做作。

definitions.definition: in a way that is artificial and not sincere
definitions.def_translation: 矫揉造作地，装模作样地;不自然地

examples.text: She laughed affectedly.
examples.translation: 她笑得很做作。

examples.text: He had a set smile and spoke in an affectedly soft voice.
examples.translation: 他笑容僵硬，用一种做作的轻柔声音说话。

more_examples.text: As he talked, his voice grew affectedly cultured.
The officer yawned affectedly.
She waved goodbye in an affectedly dramatic way.

definitions.definition: causing a strong emotion , especially sadness
definitions.def_translation: 使人感动的，动人的，激起怜悯的（尤指使人悲伤）

examples.text: It was an affecting sight.
examples.translation: 那是令人动情的一幕。

definitions.definition: a feeling of liking for a person or place

examples.text: She felt no affection for the child.
examples.translation: 她一点都不疼爱这个孩子。

examples.text: He had a deep affection for his aunt.
examples.translation: 他非常喜爱他的姑妈。

more_examples.text: There's never much display of affection between them.
filial affection
He finds it difficult to show affection.
In this society there is a taboo on any sort of public display of affection.
He remembered the teachers at his first school with great affection.

definitions.definition: feelings of liking or love :

examples.text: The former president still holds a place in the nation's affections.
examples.translation: 前总统仍深得全国人民的爱戴。

definitions.definition: to succeed in persuading someone to love you:

examples.text: Since his divorce, he has been suspicious of women who try to win his affections.

definitions.definition: showing feelings of liking or love
definitions.def_translation: 表示爱的；充满深情的；有感情的

examples.text: an affectionate kiss
examples.translation: 深情的一吻

examples.text: He's an affectionate little boy.
examples.translation: 他是个很有爱心的小男孩。

definitions.definition: in a way that shows liking or love

examples.text: She smiled affectionately at him.
examples.translation: 她亲切地对他微笑。

examples.text: He spoke affectionately about his family.
examples.translation: 他深情地谈到了他的家人。

more_examples.text: He greeted his grandchildren affectionately.
The car was affectionately known as "George".
The filmmakers speak affectionately about all of their movie's characters.

definitions.definition: feelings of liking or love

examples.text: The former president still holds a place in the nation's affections.
examples.translation: 前总统仍深得全国人民的爱戴。

examples.text: Sula seems to have transferred her affections from Jon to his brother.
examples.translation: 苏拉好像移情别恋了，不再爱乔恩，而喜欢上了他的弟弟。

examples.text: Who's the latest object of his affections?
She seemed seemed to reserve her affections primarily for animals.
